title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE PENSION FOR PRIVATE SCHOOL TEACHERS AND STAFF ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Pension for Private School Teachers and Staff Act and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof. <Amended on Feb. 28, 2000; Jun. 30, 2005>

Article 2 (Standards for recognition of survivors) (1) The standards for recognition as to whether a present or former teacher or staff member (hereafter referred to as "teachers and staff, etc.") was supporting at the time of his or her death any person falling under any of the items of Article 2(1)2 of the Pension for Private School Teachers and Staff Act (hereafter referred to as the "Act") shall be as prescribed in Appendix 1.
  (2) Pursuant to Article 2(2) of the Act, among children aged 19 or older, those who fall under survivors shall be persons with severe disabilities among persons with disabilities as defined in Article 2 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (3) In the provisions under each of the following subparagraphs, "the degree of disability prescribed by Presidential Decree" means a state in which a person is a person with severe disabilities among persons with disabilities as defined in Article 2 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. The part other than Article 2(3) of the Act and subparagraph 2 of that paragraph;
  2. Article 40(1) 4 and 5 of the Public Officials' Accident Compensation Act as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 42(1) of the Act (hereafter referred to as the "Act on accident compensation as applied");
  3. Article 57(1)4 and 5 of the Public Officials' Accident Compensation Act as applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 42(1) of the Act (hereafter referred to as the "Act on pension as applied").
  (4) Verification of the fact that a child or grandchild is a fetus shall be based on a medical certificate issued by a medical care institution under Article 24 of the Act on accident compensation as applied (hereafter referred to as a "medical care institution"). <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (5) The Teachers‘ Pension under Article 4 of the Act (hereafter referred to as the "TP") may require a child or grandchild aged 19 or older who is entitled to retirement survivors' benefits under subparagraph 2 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied or to survivors' benefits for occupational accidents under subparagraph 5 of Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied or the father of such grandchild to submit documents certifying the state of disability, in order to verify whether such person falls under a state of disability under Article 2(2), the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 2(3), or subparagraph 2 of that paragraph of the Act. <Added on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]
  [Title Amended on Jan. 14, 2025]

Article 3 (Scope of income and tax-exempt income) (1) The scope of income under Article 2(1) 4 of the Act means earned income under Article 20(1) 1 of the Income Tax Act that a teacher or staff member received after serving for a certain period at the school to which he or she belongs and the school management institution (hereafter referred to as "school institutions") and that accrued in the preceding year; provided, the Minister of Education may otherwise determine allowances etc. among earned income received from school institutions that are deemed inappropriate to be included in income for the calculation of contributions and benefits. <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (2) The scope of tax-exempt income under Article 2(1)4 of the Act means tax-exempt income of the preceding year under subparagraph 3 of Article 12 of the Income Tax Act. <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 3-2 (Determination of standard monthly income) (1) The TP shall determine the standard monthly income of teachers and staff on July 1 each year; provided, the standard monthly income of teachers and staff newly appointed in that year shall be determined at the time of such new appointment. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018; Jan. 14, 2025>
  (2) Where a teacher or staff member engaged in income-earning activities for 1 month or longer in the preceding year, the standard monthly income of such teacher or staff member shall be the amount calculated by multiplying by 30 the amount obtained by dividing the income under Article 3(1) minus tax-exempt income under Article 3(2) by the total number of days during which such income-earning activities were carried out in the preceding year and adding the amount calculated by multiplying such result by the rate of increase in remuneration of public officials for that year as publicly announced pursuant to Article 5(5) of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension Act. <Amended on Nov. 29, 2013; Sep. 18, 2018; Jul. 7, 2025>
  (3) The standard monthly income of teachers and staff who were appointed in the preceding year and whose period of engagement in income-earning activities in that year was less than 1 month and of teachers and staff newly appointed in the relevant year shall be the amount equal to 30 times the amount obtained by dividing the amount remaining after excluding tax-exempt income under Article 3(2) from earned income under Article 20(1)1 of the Income Tax Act to be paid to such teachers and staff by their affiliated school institutions in that year by the total number of days during which income-earning activities will be carried out in that year. <Amended on Nov. 29, 2013; Sep. 18, 2018>
  (4) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) and (3), where a teacher or staff member had a period of leave of absence or a period of work converted to a part-time selection system during the preceding year, the standard monthly income of such teacher or staff member shall be the amount obtained by adding the amount calculated by multiplying the most recently applied standard monthly income by the rate of increase in remuneration of public officials for that year. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  (5) Where a school institution fails to submit income-related data pursuant to Article 3-5(1) and no income-related data are available, the standard monthly income of the relevant teacher or staff member shall be the amount corresponding to each of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012; Sep. 18, 2018>
  1. In the case of an incumbent teacher or staff member: The amount obtained by adjusting the standard monthly income of such teacher or staff member for the preceding year in accordance with the rate of increase in remuneration of public officials;
  2. In the case of a newly appointed teacher or staff member: The smallest amount among the standard monthly incomes of the teacher and staff member who fall under similar job categories or positions at school institutions of the same level as the affiliated school institution.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 3-3 (Lower limit of standard monthly income) (1) The lower limit of the standard monthly income under Article 2(1)4 of the Act shall be the amount corresponding to each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Kindergarten teachers and elementary and secondary school teachers: KRW 922,000;
  2. University teachers (including junior college teachers): KRW 1,208,400;
  3. General and technical administrative staff: KRW 820,100;
  4. Functional administrative staff: KRW 735,100;
  5. Employment-based administrative staff: KRW 525,400.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the Minister of Education may adjust the lower limits under each subparagraph of paragraph (1) where there is a significant change in the living standards, wages, prices, or other economic conditions of teachers and staff. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  (3) The Minister of Education shall, when adjusting the lower limit pursuant to paragraph (2), promptly announce the adjusted lower limit and the reasons for adjustment. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  [This Article Added on Jan. 26, 2012]
  [Previous Article 3-3 moved to Article 3-4 <Jan. 26, 2012>]

Article 3-4 (Period of application of standard monthly income) The standard monthly income shall apply from July of the relevant year to June of the following year; provided, where Article 3-2(3) applies, it shall apply for the period corresponding to each of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  1. Where a teacher or staff member was appointed in the preceding year and the period of engagement in income-earning activities in that year was less than one month: From the date of appointment to June 30 of the year after the year following the year in which the date of appointment falls;
  2. Where a teacher or staff member was newly appointed in the relevant year: From the date of appointment to June 30 of the year following the year in which the date of appointment falls.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]
  [Moved from Article 3-3; previous Article 3-4 moved to Article 3-5 <Jan. 26, 2012>]

Article 3-5 (Submission of income-related data and notification of standard monthly income) (1) In order to determine the standard monthly income of teachers and staff affiliated with the relevant school institution, the head of a school institution shall submit income-related data to the TP pursuant to Article 19 of the Act in accordance with each of the following subparagraphs; provided, where statements of payment, etc. under Article 164 of the Income Tax Act have been reported to the National Tax Service, the submission of income-related data may be omitted:
  1. Teachers and staff who engaged in earned income for 1 month or longer in the preceding year: Earned income data under Article 3(1) shall be submitted by the end of May each year;
  2. Teachers and staff who engaged in earned income for less than 1 month in the preceding year (excluding those on leave of absence and those who returned to work): Estimated earned income data for the relevant year shall be submitted by the end of May of that year;
  3. Teachers and staff newly appointed in the relevant year: Estimated earned income data for the relevant year shall be submitted at the time of reporting such new appointment.
  (2) Where the standard monthly income for each teacher or staff member is determined, the TP shall notify the head of the relevant school institution of such amount and the contributions corresponding thereto.
  [This Article added on Jan. 1, 2010]
  [Moved from Article 3-4; previous Article 3-5 moved to Article 3-6 <Jan. 26, 2012>]

Article 3-6 (Conversion of standard monthly income and average standard monthly income into present value) (1) The method of converting the standard monthly income under the main clause of Article 2(1)5 of the Act into present value shall be a method of converting it into the present value at the time when the cause for benefits arises by successively multiplying the standard monthly income by the rate of increase in remuneration of public officials for each applicable period.
  (2) The method of converting the average standard monthly income under the proviso of Article 2(1)5 of the Act into present value shall be a method of converting it into the present value at the time when payment of the pension begins by successively multiplying the average standard monthly income by the rate of increase in remuneration of public officials for each year.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Apr. 29, 2014]

Article 3-7 (Verification of reported income) (1) Where income-related data submitted by a school institution pursuant to Article 3-5(1) fall under any of the following subparagraphs and it is deemed that there has been understatement, overstatement, or omission of income, the TP shall request the Commissioner of the National Tax Service to provide the income-related data of the relevant person and verify such data: <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012>
  1. Where the income is distinctly lower or higher than the average income of other teachers and staff who fall under similar job categories, positions, etc.;
  2. Where the income differs from the contents of wage ledgers or other income-related documents or books, etc.
  (2) Where the income-related data submitted pursuant to Article 3-5(1) show a distinct difference from the income verified pursuant to paragraph (1), the TP shall determine the standard monthly income on the basis of the data verified pursuant to paragraph (1). <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012>
  [This Article added on Jan. 1, 2010]
  [Moved from Article 3-6 <Jan. 26, 2012>]

CHAPTER II KOREA TEACHERS PENSION

Article 4 (Registration of establishment) The matters to be registered upon the establishment of Korea Teachers' Pension shall be as follows: <Amended on Feb. 28, 2000; Jan. 1, 2010>
  1. Purpose;
  2. Name;
  3. Location of the principal office and its branches;
  4. Names and addresses of executive officers;
  5. Method of public notice.

Article 5 (Registration of establishment of branches) Where the TP establishes a branch pursuant to Article 6 of the Act, it shall, within 2 weeks from the date of such establishment, register the name, location, and date of establishment of the established branch at the location of the principal office.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 21, 2025]

Article 6 (Registration of relocation) (1) Where the TP relocates its principal office, it shall register the new location and the date of relocation at the former location or the new location within 2 weeks from the date of such relocation.
  (2) Where the TP relocates a branch, it shall register the new location and the date of relocation at the location of the principal office within 2 weeks from the date of such relocation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 21, 2025]

Article 7 (Registration of changes) Where the TP changes any of the matters to be registered under each subparagraph of Article 4 or Article 5 (excluding cases falling under registration of relocation under Article 6), it shall register such changes at the location of the principal office within 2 weeks from the date of such change.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 21, 2025]

Article 8 (Applicant for registration) With respect to the registration of the TP and its branches, the chairperson of the TP shall be the applicant; provided, this shall not apply to the registration of establishment of the TP. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 9 (Documents to be attached to application for registration) (1) The application for registration of establishment of the TP under Article 5(2) of the Act shall be accompanied by each of the following documents: <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>
  1. A copy of the articles of incorporation;
  2. Documents certifying the appointment of executive officers.
  (2) An application for registration under Articles 6 and 7 shall be accompanied by documents certifying the change in matters to be registered.

Article 10 (Commencement of registration period) Where any matter to be registered under the Act and this Decree requires authorization or approval from the Minister of Education, the registration period shall be calculated from the date on which the written authorization or approval reaches the TP. <Amended on Feb. 1, 1991; Jan. 29, 2001; Feb. 29, 2008; Jan. 1, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 11 (Competent registry offices) (1) The registration of the TP shall be handled by the district court, branch court, or registry office having jurisdiction over the location of the principal office. <Amended on Jan. 21, 2025>
  (2) A registration book for the Korea Teachers' Pension shall be kept at the registry office. <Amended on Feb. 24, 2003; Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 12 (Mutatis mutandis application) Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Decree with respect to the registration of the TP, the relevant provisions of the Non-Contentious Case Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis; in such cases, "head office" shall be deemed "principal office," and "branch office" shall be deemed "branch." <Amended on Jun. 30, 2005; Jan. 1, 2010>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Feb. 2, 1996]

Article 13 (Scope of profit-making activities) The scope of activities for profit prescribed in Article 16 of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Activities in which profit seeking is evident by independently operating commercial, industrial, financial, or other profit-making businesses;
  2. Becoming an officer such as a director, auditor, unlimited liability partner executing business, manager, promoter, or other executive officer of an enterprise falling under subparagraph 1;
  3. Investing in the enterprise of another person that is related to one's duties;
  4. Other activities continuously conducted for the purpose of gaining profit.

Article 13-2 (Request for provision of data) (1) "Data prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19(4)9 of the Act means the data under subparagraph 1 of Appendix 2.
  (2) The parties from whom the TP (including persons entrusted with the affairs of the TP pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree) may request the provision of data under subparagraph 9 of Article 19(4) of the Act shall be as set forth in subparagraph 2 of Appendix 2.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 14 (Entrustment of affairs) Where the TP intends to entrust its affairs to postal agencies, local governments, financial institutions, public enterprises under Article 5 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or other persons pursuant to Article 20 of the Act, it shall determine by agreement with the person to whom the affairs are to be entrusted the scope of the affairs to be entrusted, processing procedures, entrustment fees, and other necessary matters. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 15 Deleted. <Feb. 28, 2000>

Article 16 Deleted. <Feb. 28, 2000>

CHAPTER III AGGREGATION OF PERIOD OF SERVICE

Article 17 Deleted. <Mar. 27, 1989>

Article 17-2 (Service periods recognized as periods of service) "Period of service prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 31(2)1 of the Act means the following periods: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2005, Dec. 7, 2009, Jan. 1, 2010, Dec. 4, 2013, Nov. 29, 2016, Sep. 18, 2018, Jun. 30, 2020>
  1. A period during which a person called for defense or for full time reserve service has served;
  2. A period during which a person has served as social service personnel or international cooperation service personnel pursuant to a call-up for supplementary service (limited to the period calculated pursuant to Article 151 of the Enforcement Decree of the Military Service Act);
  3. A period during which a person served as alternative service personnel pursuant to a call-up for alternative service (limited to the period calculated pursuant to Article 151 of the Enforcement Decree of the Military Service Act).
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2000]

Article 17-3 (Procedure for inclusion of service periods prior to appointment) (1) An application for inclusion of service periods pursuant to Article 31-2 of the Act shall be submitted after appointment and no later than the day before the date of retirement.
  (2) Where the TP receives an application for inclusion of service periods pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall decide whether to include such service periods and notify the applicant and the head of the relevant school institution of the result.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 14, 2025]

Article 18 (Procedure for aggregation of periods of service) (1) A person who intends to have periods of service aggregated pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Act shall submit to the TP, after appointment and no later than the day before the date of retirement, an application for approval of aggregation of periods of service stating the periods of service to be aggregated and the method of payment of the amount of remuneration and interest to be refunded (hereafter referred to as "refund") that is required to be returned; provided, where a retired teacher or staff member is reappointed as a teacher or staff member without claiming retirement benefits, the submission of an application for approval of aggregation of periods of service may be replaced by indicating the intent to apply for aggregation of periods of service in the report of appointment of teachers and staff submitted by the head of the relevant school institution to the TP pursuant to Article 89-2. <Amended on Jun. 25, 1976; Dec. 31, 1977; Jun. 23, 1981; Dec. 31, 1982; Mar. 27, 1989; Feb. 2, 1996; Dec. 30, 2000; Jun. 30, 2005; Jan. 24, 2007; Jan. 1, 2010; Nov. 29, 2013; Sep. 18, 2018; Jan. 14, 2025>
  (2) Deleted. <Nov. 29, 2013>
  (3) Where the TP receives an application under paragraph (1), it shall, after examining the period to be aggregated, the amount of refund, and other necessary matters, decide whether to approve the aggregation of periods of service and notify the applicant and the head of the relevant school institution thereof. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010; Nov. 29, 2013>

Article 19 (Method of payment of refund) (1) Payment of the refund by a person whose aggregation of periods of service has been approved shall, in the case of a lump-sum refund, be made by the end of the month following the month in which approval of aggregation was granted, and in the case of installment refund, be made from the month following the month in which approval of aggregation was granted either by paying to the head of the relevant school institution at the time of receipt of remuneration or by paying by the end of the relevant month to postal agencies, etc. to which the TP entrusts its affairs pursuant to Article 14. <Amended on Jun. 23, 1981; Dec. 31, 1982; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) Installment payment of the refund shall be made on a monthly basis, and the number of installments shall be as desired by the person whose aggregation has been approved, within a limit of 60 installments. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  (3) Deleted. <Mar. 27, 1989>
  (4) Where a person whose aggregation of periods of service has been approved retires or dies and there remains any unpaid refund, the TP may deduct the unpaid refund and pay the benefits. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>

Article 20 (Calculation of refund amount) (1) In calculating the refund amount, the period for calculating interest to be additionally collected on the amount of remuneration to be refunded shall be based on the number of months from the month following the month in which such remuneration was paid to the month in which the application for approval of aggregation of periods of service is received by the TP, and such interest shall be included in the amount of remuneration on an annual basis for the calculation of subsequent interest; provided, in the case of installment payment pursuant to Article 32(3) of the Act, the period for calculating interest to be additionally collected shall be from the month following the month in which aggregation of periods of service was approved to the month in which installment payment is completed, and the amount of each installment to be paid shall be the amount obtained by equally dividing the principal and interest according to the number of installments. <Amended on Mar. 27, 1989; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 1, 2010; Nov. 29, 2013; Jul. 2, 2019>
  (2) The interest rate under paragraph (1) shall be the highest interest rate on time deposits applied by banks established under the Banking Act that operate nationwide (hereafter referred to as "nationwide banks") as of January 1 of each year during the interest calculation period. <Amended on Mar. 27, 1989; Feb. 2, 1996; Dec. 30, 2000; Jun. 30, 2005; Nov. 15, 2010>
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), where installment payment is made pursuant to Article 32(3) of the Act, the interest rate to be applied shall be the interest rate as of January 1 of the year in which aggregation of periods of service was approved; provided, where the difference between the interest rate during installment payment and the interest rate at the time aggregation of periods of service was approved becomes 2 percent or more, the refund shall be recalculated by applying the increased or decreased interest rate, and the same shall apply where there is again an increase or decrease of 2 percent or more compared with the changed interest rate during installment payment. <Added on Dec. 30, 2000>
  (4) Where a refund is not paid by the payment deadline under Article 19 (1), the period for calculating delinquency interest shall be the period of arrears (calculated on a daily basis), and the interest rate shall be a rate equivalent to twice the highest interest rate on 1-year time deposits applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each year during the delinquency interest calculation period. <Added on Dec. 30, 2000; Jun. 30, 2005; Nov. 29, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 1982]

CHAPTER IV BENEFITS

SECTION 1 General Provisions

Article 21 (Benefits subject to deliberation) "The types of benefits prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 34(1) of the Act mean the following benefits: <Amended on Sep. 29, 2021>
  1. Nursing care benefits, assistive devices, or assistive device allowances under Article 33-2 of the Act;
  2. The following benefits under the Act on accident compensation as applied:
  a. Medical care benefits under Article 22 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  b. Disability pension or disability lump-sum payment under Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  c. On-duty survivors' pension under Article 36 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  d. On-duty survivors' compensation under Article 37 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  3. Off-duty disability pension or off-duty disability lump sum under Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 21-2 (Pension Benefit Examination Committee for Private School Teachers and Staff) (1) The Pension Benefit Examination Committee for Private School Teachers and Staff (hereinafter referred to as the "Benefit Examination Committee") shall be established within the TP pursuant to the proviso of Article 34(1) of the Act.
  (2) The following matters shall be subject to deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Whether to recognize re-treatment pursuant to Article 33-3 of the Act and Article 32-3 of this Decree;
  2. Determination of benefits pursuant to the proviso of Article 34(1) of the Act;
  3. Whether to wholly or partially refrain from exercising the right to claim damages against a third party pursuant to the proviso of the main clause of Article 41(2) of the Act;
  4. Whether grounds for restriction of benefits apply pursuant to Article 44(3) and (4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied and Article 63(3) and (4) of the Act on pension as applied;
  5. Whether to terminate medical care pursuant to Article 32-7;
  6. Whether a disability state applies, determination and revision of disability grades pursuant to Articles 41, 44, and 45 (including cases where other provisions follow or apply mutatis mutandis the relevant provisions with respect to disability states, etc.).
  (3) The Benefit Examination Committee shall be composed of not more than 50 members, including one chairperson.
  (4) The chairperson of the Benefit Examination Committee shall be a standing director of the TP, and the members other than the chairperson shall be appointed by the chairperson of the TP from among public officials of Grade 5 or higher of the Ministry of Education (including general service public officials belonging to the Senior Executive Service), teachers and staff, and persons engaged in medical services or legal affairs.
  (5) The term of office of members of the Benefit Examination Committee (excluding the chairperson) shall be 2 years; provided, where a member who is a public official of the Ministry of Education retires or is transferred, his or her term of office shall expire, and a new member shall be appointed from among public officials of the Ministry of Education.
  (6) The chairperson of the TP may dismiss a member of the Benefit Examination Committee where such member falls under any of the following cases:
  1. Where the member becomes unable to perform his or her duties due to a physical or mental disorder;
  2. Where there is misconduct related to the performance of duties;
  3. Where the member is deemed unfit to serve as a member of the Benefit Examination Committee due to neglect of duties, impairment of dignity, or other reasons;
  4. Where the member expresses his or her intention that it is difficult to perform his or her duties.
  (7) The chairperson of the Benefit Examination Committee shall convene meetings and preside over them; provided, where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall perform such duties, and where there is no such designated member or where the designated member is unable to perform such duties, the eldest member shall perform such duties.
  (8) Each meeting of the Benefit Examination Committee shall be composed of not fewer than 9 and not more than 11 members, including the chairperson of the Benefit Examination Committee and members designated for each meeting by the chairperson.
  (9) A meeting of the Benefit Examination Committee shall be opened with the attendance of a majority of the members constituting the meeting pursuant to paragraph (8) (including cases where members attend by accessing information and communications networks such as the internet where prompt deliberation is required or the matter is minor), and resolutions shall be adopted with the consent of a majority of the members present.
  (10) The TP may pay allowances to members who attend meetings of the Benefit Examination Committee within the budgetary limits; provided, this shall not apply where a member who is a public official attends a meeting in direct connection with his or her official duties.
  (11) Matters necessary for the operation of the Benefit Examination Committee and its meetings, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (10), shall be determined by the chairperson of the TP.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22 (Upper limit of standard monthly income) (1) "Amount prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the latter part of Article 35(1) of the Act means the standard monthly income corresponding to each of the following subparagraphs; provided, where the upper limit of the standard monthly income for the relevant year is lower than that for the preceding year, the upper limit of the standard monthly income for the preceding year shall apply: <Amended on Jan. 26, 2012>
  1. In the case of teachers: The highest standard monthly income among the standard monthly incomes of university presidents to whom Appendix 12 to the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations applies;
  2. In the case of administrative staff: The highest standard monthly income among the standard monthly incomes of Grade 2 public officials in general service to whom Appendix 3 to the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations applies.
  (2) The Minister of Education shall notify the TP of the upper limit of the standard monthly income under paragraph (1) by May 31 of each year. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 22-2 (Conversion of average standard monthly income of all public officials into present value)

Article 22-3 (Issuance of pension certificate) (1) The TP shall issue a pension certificate to a person who receives pension-type benefits (hereafter referred to as a "pension beneficiary").
  (2) Where a pension beneficiary loses or damages a pension certificate, he or she may receive a reissued pension certificate from the TP. In such cases, where reissuance is made on the grounds of damage, the damaged pension certificate shall be returned to the TP.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22-4 (Report of change of address or name of pension beneficiary) Where a pension beneficiary changes his or her address or name, he or she shall report such change to the TP in accordance with each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Where the address is changed: By submitting a report of change of address to the TP or by making an oral report;
  2. Where the name is changed: By submitting a report of change of name together with a copy of a resident registration transcript or a basic certificate of family relations.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22-5 (Date of payment of pensions) Pursuant to Article 13(3) of the Act on accident compensation as applied and Article 34(3) of the Act on pension as applied, the payment date of pension-type benefits shall be the 25th day of each month; provided, where the payment date falls on a Saturday or a public holiday, payment shall be made on the preceding day, and where the right to receive a pension is extinguished, payment may be made before the payment date.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22-6 (Claim for pension settlement due to emigration or loss of nationality) (1) Where a pension beneficiary who emigrates to a foreign country intends to receive a lump sum in lieu of pension-type benefits pursuant to Article 15(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 36(1) of the Act on pension as applied, he or she shall submit to the TP an application for pension settlement together with documents proving emigration such as a confirmation of overseas emigration report under Article 5(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Emigration Act. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (2) Where a pension beneficiary who has lost nationality intends to receive a lump sum in lieu of pension-type benefits pursuant to Article 15(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 36 (2) of the Act on pension as applied, he or she shall submit to the TP an application for pension settlement together with documents proving loss of nationality such as a removal register transcript or a basic certificate among certificates of family relations records.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22-7 (Institutions subject to full suspension of pension payments) Pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied and the main clause of the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 50(1) of the Act on pension as applied, where a beneficiary is employed as an executive officer or employee, the institutions referred to in Article 50(1)3 through 5 of the Act on pension as applied, for which payment of disability pension under Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied and retirement pension or early retirement pension under Article 43 of the Act on pension as applied or off-duty disability pension under Article 59 of the same Act (hereafter referred to as "retirement pensions, etc.") is fully suspended, shall be institutions designated and publicly announced pursuant to Article 46(5) of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension Act.

Article 22-8 (Suspension of payment of disability pension) (1) Where a beneficiary of retirement pensions, etc. (hereafter in this Article referred to as a "beneficiary of retirement pensions, etc.") is appointed as or retires from a private school teacher or staff member, a public official, or a soldier to whom the Act, the Public Officials Pension Act, or the Military Pension Act applies, he or she shall obtain confirmation from the head of the relevant pension-handling institution or the head of the relevant institution within 10 days and submit to the TP a report of reappointment or a report of re-retirement.
  (2) The monthly income amount under the former part of the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 50(3) of the Act on pension as applied shall be the amount obtained by dividing the annual income amount for 1 year from January 1 to December 31 (amounts of less than KRW 10,000 shall be disregarded) by the number of months in which such income was earned. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (3) Where, pursuant to the former part of the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 50(3) of the Act on pension as applied, the monthly income amount for the relevant year exceeds the average monthly pension amount of public officials for the preceding year, payment of retirement pensions, etc. shall be partially suspended; the amount to be suspended shall be provisionally calculated by applying the average monthly pension amount of public officials for the preceding year and shall be settled after a final tax base return is filed pursuant to paragraph (5).
  (4) The TP shall suspend payment of retirement pensions, etc. for the relevant year on the basis of data provided pursuant to Article 19(4) of the Act; provided, where the income amount of a beneficiary of retirement pensions, etc. cannot be verified based on data provided by State agencies, etc., payment of retirement pensions, etc. shall be suspended on the basis of the income amount for the preceding year or the year before the preceding year.
  (5) Where the TP suspends payment of retirement pensions, etc. pursuant to Article 50 of the Act on pension as applied, it shall finalize the amount of pension payment suspension for the relevant year after a final tax base return is filed pursuant to Article 70 of the Income Tax Act and add or subtract the settlement difference when paying retirement pensions, etc. from the following month onward; provided, where a beneficiary of retirement pensions, etc. requests adjustment of the amount of pension payment suspension by submitting an application for adjustment of the amount of pension payment suspension together with objective materials capable of proving income for the relevant year, the amount of pension payment suspension may be adjusted before a final tax base return is filed. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (6) Where it is confirmed that a beneficiary of retirement pensions, etc. has no income other than retirement pensions, etc. in the month in which the settlement difference under the main sentence of paragraph (5) is deducted from retirement pensions, etc., the settlement difference shall be deducted within the limit of 20 percent of the monthly pension amount.
  (7) The average standard monthly income of all public officials for the preceding year under the proviso of the main clause other than the subparagraphs of Article 50(1) of the Act on pension as applied shall be the amount calculated in May of the preceding year and shall apply from January through December of the relevant year.
  (8) The Minister of Education shall notify the TP of the average monthly pension amount of public officials for the preceding year under Article 50(3) of the Act on pension as applied by January 10 of each year.
  (9) "Degree of disability prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 32(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied and Article 61(2) of the Act on pension as applied means, respectively, a state of disability falling under disability grades 1 through 14 under Article 41 of this Decree and Appendices 5 and 6.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 22-9 (Investigation into personal status of pension beneficiaries) (1) In order to identify changes in personal status that affect pension-type benefits, the TP may request a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (referring to the head of an autonomous Gu; hereafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over the residence or place of registration of a pension beneficiary to conduct an investigation into such beneficiary's personal status.
  (2) A Special Self-Governing City Mayor, Special Self-Governing Province Governor, or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu who receives a request for investigation under paragraph (1) (hereafter referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") shall conduct such investigation without delay and notify the TP of the results thereof.
  (3) The TP may, in order to verify changes in or extinction of entitlement, etc. pursuant to Article 19(1) and (2) of the Act, conduct investigations into matters such as the death, divorce, maintenance, or fulfillment of child-rearing responsibilities of a beneficiary by targeting the beneficiary or his or her family members, etc., or may request submission of data related thereto. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (4) A beneficiary residing abroad shall, as of May 31 of each year, have documents stating changes in personal status confirmed by the head of an overseas diplomatic mission (referring to the head of an overseas diplomatic mission located in a neighboring country in the case of a country where no overseas diplomatic mission is established) and submit them to the TP by June 30 of each year.
  (5) Where a beneficiary fails to submit data under paragraph (3) or (4) without a compelling reason, the TP may suspend payment of benefits pursuant to Article 19 (3) of the Act. In such cases, the TP shall notify the beneficiary or his or her family members, etc. in advance, before suspending payment of benefits, that payment of benefits may be suspended if the data under paragraph (3) or (4) is not submitted.
  (6) Where the grounds for suspension of payment of benefits under paragraph (5) are resolved, the TP shall immediately resume payment.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 23 (Method of payment of benefits to representative of survivors) (1) Where there are 2 or more persons of the same order of priority among survivors who are entitled to receive any of the following benefits and a representative has been designated from among such persons of the same order of priority or their legal representatives and receipt of the relevant benefits has been entrusted to such representative on behalf of all such persons, the TP may pay the full amount to the representative instead of paying the benefits in equal shares, pursuant to Article 37 of the Act:
  1. Survivors' benefits for occupational accidents under subparagraph 5 of Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  2. Retirement survivors' benefits under subparagraph 2 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied.
  (2) Delegation under paragraph (1) shall be made by submitting to the TP a written designation of a representative personally signed by the delegating person, with documents attached according to each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Where the delegating person is an adult: A copy of the delegator's own identification card, such as a resident registration card;
  2. Where the delegating person is a minor: A copy of the identification card, such as a resident registration card, of his or her legal representative.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 24 (Special cases for payment of benefits where there are no survivors) (1) "Amount within the limit prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the first part of Article 38 (1) of the Act means the amount classified as follows:
  1. Pension-type benefits: An amount obtained by multiplying 3 years' worth of the original pension amount as of the time of death by the following ratio (where teachers and staff, etc. died before reaching the retirement pension eligibility age under Article 43(1) 1 through 4 of the Act on pension as applied, the amount equivalent to the early retirement pension as of the time of death shall apply; and where a person died after exceeding the 5-year shortfall period under Article 43(2) of the same Act, the amount equivalent to the early retirement pension calculated on the assumption that the person died after exceeding 4 years but within 5 years of the shortfall period shall apply):
  36?Number of months during which the pension could have been received until death pursuant to Article 43 (1) of the Act on pension as applied or Article 13 (1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied?/36
  2. Other benefits: The full amount of the original benefit; provided, on-duty survivors' compensation under Article 37 of the Act on accident compensation as applied and lump-sum retirement survivors' pension and retirement survivors' lump-sum payment under Articles 54 and 58 of the Act on pension as applied shall be 1/2 of the original benefit amount.
  (2) Where teachers and staff, etc. die leaving neither survivors nor lineal ascendants or descendants, the TP may pay the benefits under paragraph (1) to the head of the school institution to which the deceased teachers and staff, etc. belonged, so that such benefits may be used to provide a grave, ritual vessels, a memorial monument, etc. for the deceased teacher or staff member, etc., or to cover the costs of commemorative projects, etc. or medical care costs incurred before death.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 24-2 (Payment of benefits) (1) Benefits shall be paid by using the deposit account of the person entitled to receive benefits opened at a financial institution entrusted with the payment of benefits by the TP pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree; provided, where it is especially necessary for the protection of rights under Article 40 of the Act, the TP may determine otherwise. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) Benefits deposited into the deposit account of the person entitled to receive benefits pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be deemed to have been received by the person himself or herself.
  [This Article Added on Feb. 24, 2003]

Article 25 (Recovery of benefits) (1) The interest and recovery costs to be added to and collected together with the benefit amount pursuant to the latter part of the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 39 of the Act shall be as follows; in such cases, the period for calculating interest to be added to the benefit amount shall be from the day following the day on which the benefits were received to the day on which the amount of benefits to be recovered and the interest thereon (hereafter referred to as "amount to be recovered") are determined and notified, and such interest shall be included in the benefit amount on an annual basis for the calculation of subsequent interest amounts:
  1. Interest: An amount calculated by applying, for each year, the highest interest rate on time deposits applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of the relevant year;
  2. Recovery costs: An amount calculated by the TP as travel expenses necessary for investigations related to recovery of benefits and other costs incurred for recovery.
  (2) Where a person required to pay the amount to be recovered pursuant to the latter part of the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 39 of the Act fails to make payment by the payment deadline, the delinquency interest shall be the amount calculated by applying, for each year during the delinquency interest calculation period, an interest rate equivalent to twice the highest interest rate on time deposits applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of the relevant year. In such cases, the delinquency interest calculation period shall be from the day following the payment deadline of the amount to be recovered to the day on which such amount is paid.
  (3) A person who has received benefits or the head of a school institution shall, upon becoming aware of any fact falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 39 of the Act, report or notify the TP thereof without delay.
  (4) Where the TP becomes aware of grounds for recovery of benefits through a report or notification under paragraph (3) or by any other means, it shall investigate such grounds without delay, send a notice of payment of the amount to be recovered to the person who received the benefits, and notify the head of the relevant school institution thereof.
  (5) A person who receives a notice of payment under paragraph (4) shall pay the amount to be recovered within 30 days from the date of receipt of such notice; provided, in cases falling under subparagraphs 3 and 4 of Article 39 of the Act, such person may, upon submitting to the TP an application for installment payment of the amount to be recovered and obtaining approval therefor, pay the amount in monthly installments from the month following the month in which approval is granted, within the limits set forth in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Where the amount to be returned is less than KRW 10,000,000: 8 installments;
  2. Where the amount to be returned is at least KRW 10,000,000 but less than KRW 20,000,000: 16 installments;
  3. Where the amount to be returned is at least KRW 20,000,000 but less than KRW 40,000,000: 32 installments;
  4. Where the amount to be returned is at least KRW 40,000,000 but less than KRW 60,000,000: 48 installments;
  5. Where the amount to be returned is at least KRW 60,000,000: 60 installments.
  (6) Where installment payment is made pursuant to the proviso of the part other than the subparagraphs of paragraph (5), the interest to be added (excluding cases falling under subparagraph 4 of Article 39 of the Act where benefits were incorrectly paid from the outset due to an error or omission of the head of a school institution or the TP) shall be calculated by applying the interest rate under paragraph (1) 1 to the amount to be recovered payable during the installment period. In such cases, the amount of each installment shall be the amount obtained by equally dividing the principal and interest according to the number of installments.
  (7) Where a person whose installment payment of the amount to be recovered has been approved pursuant to the proviso of the part other than the subparagraphs of paragraph (5) is in arrears with installment payments for 3 months or more, the TP may cancel the approval for installment payment and recover the amount to be recovered and the delinquency interest in a lump sum.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 26 (Security for the right to receive benefits) (1) "Financial institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 40(1) 1 of the Act means financial institutions falling under Article 87-2(1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 27 (Claim for payment of amounts deducted under other statutes or regulations) (1) Where a school management institution intends to receive the amount deducted by the TP pursuant to Article 41(1) of the Act, it shall apply to the TP by stating the grounds for payment of the benefits paid by the relevant school management institution to teachers and staff, the personal details of the teachers and staff who received such benefits, and the amount paid. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) Where the TP receives an application under paragraph (1), it shall verify the relevant facts and pay the deducted amount to the school management institution without delay. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 27-2 (Verification of beneficiary status for pension adjustment) (1) For the purpose of adjustment pursuant to Article 20(6) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 41(2) of the Act on pension as applied, the TP may request the Government Employees Pension Service, the Minister of National Defense, or the Specific Post Office Pension Service Agency to verify whether a person entitled to receive benefits payable to survivors is a beneficiary of a retirement pension, early retirement pension, or retired service pension under the Public Officials Pension Act, the Military Pension Act, or the Special Post Offices Act.
  (2) Where the Government Employees Pension Service, the Minister of National Defense, or the Special Post Offices Pension Management Agency receives a request under paragraph (1), it shall verify whether the relevant person is entitled to receive a retirement pension, early retirement pension, or retired service pension under the Public Officials Pension Act, the Military Pension Act, or the Special Post Offices Act, and notify the TP of the results.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 28 (Adjustment with third-party compensation for damages) (1) Where a teacher or staff member sustains an injury, contracts a disease, becomes disabled, or dies (hereafter in this Article referred to as "injury, etc.") due to a harmful act of a third party, the persons entitled to receive any of the following benefits and the medical care institution that provided medical care shall, without delay, report to the head of the relevant school institution the fact that the injury, etc. occurred due to a harmful act of a third party: <Amended on Sep. 29, 2021>
  1. Nursing care benefits, assistive devices, and assistive device allowances under Article 33-2 of the Act;
  2. On-duty medical care benefits, rehabilitation benefits, disability benefits, and on-duty survivors' compensation under Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  3. Off-duty disability benefits under subparagraph 3 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied.
  (2) Where the head of a school institution receives a report under paragraph (1), he or she shall, without delay, investigate the circumstances of the harmful act and matters concerning compensation for damages under the Compulsory Motor Vehicle Liability Security Act and other statutes or regulations, and send the results thereof to the TP.
  (3) Where a beneficiary did not receive compensation for damages from the third party who committed the harmful act at the time of claiming the benefits under paragraph (1) but thereafter receives compensation for damages from such third party after receiving the relevant benefits, he or she shall immediately report such fact to the TP and submit documents related to compensation for damages.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 28-2 (Change in types of benefits and timing of payment) (1) A person who intends to make any change falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall submit an application for such change to the TP before commencement of payment of benefits or within 30 days from the benefit payment date (in the case of pension-type benefits, meaning the initial payment date):
  1. Change in the type of benefits falling under any of the following items:
  a. Disability benefits under subparagraph 3 of Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  b. Survivors' benefits for occupational accidents under subparagraph 5 of Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  c. Retirement benefits under subparagraph 1 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied;
  d. Retirement survivors' benefits under subparagraph 2 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied;
  2. Change in the timing of payment of early retirement pension under Article 43(2) of the Act on pension as applied.
  (2) Where any change is made pursuant to an application under paragraph (1), any benefits already received shall be returned together with interest calculated for the number of days from the day following the day on which such benefits were received to the day of return (the highest interest rate on time deposits applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each relevant year shall apply).
  (3) Where the type of benefits falling under subparagraphs 1 and 2 of Article 28 of the Act on pension as applied is changed pursuant to an application under paragraph (1), or the timing of payment of early retirement pension under Article 43(2) of the same Act is changed, a person who has claimed installment pension pursuant to Article 45 of the same Act, a person who has filed an advance claim for installment pension pursuant to Article 48 of the same Act, or a person who has filed an installment claim for retirement pension lump sum, etc. pursuant to Article 49 of the same Act shall be deemed to have likewise applied for a change in the type of benefits or the timing of payment.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

SECTION 2 Benefits Pursuant to the Act on Accident Compensation as Applied

Subsection 1 On-duty Medical Care Benefits

Article 29 (On-duty medical care benefits) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. undergo medical care due to an on-duty disaster (including cases of re-treatment pursuant to Article 33-3 of the Act), the TP shall pay medical care benefits under Article 22 of the Act on accident compensation as applied after deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee (hereafter referred to as "on-duty medical care benefits").
  (2) "On-duty disaster" in paragraph (1) means a case falling under any of the following subparagraphs, and the detailed standards for recognition thereof shall be as set forth in Appendix 3; provided, where there is no substantial causal relationship between the duties and the injury or disease, such case shall not be deemed an on-duty disaster:
  1. On-duty injury: An injury resulting from an accident falling under any of the following items (hereafter referred to as an "on-duty accident"):
  a. An accident occurring in the course of performing duties or acts incidental thereto;
  b. An accident occurring while commuting to or from work by the ordinary route and method;
  c. Any other accident occurring in connection with the performance of duties;
  2. On-duty disease: A disease falling under any of the following items:
  a. A disease caused by physical, chemical, or biological factors in the course of performing duties;
  b. A disease caused by duties imposing physical or mental burden in the course of performing duties;
  c. A disease caused by an on-duty injury;
  d. Any other disease occurring in connection with the performance of duties.
  (3) Where, during medical care for an on-duty disaster, an additional injury or disease caused by such on-duty disaster is newly discovered in teachers and staff, etc. and requires medical care, such additionally discovered injury or disease shall be deemed an on-duty disaster.
  (4) In the course of treatment for an on-duty injury or disease, where complications are induced with such injury or disease being the principal cause, such complications shall be deemed an on-duty disease; provided, where the complications are naturally induced or aggravated due to an underlying disease or constitutional causes, such complications shall not be deemed an on-duty disease.
  (5) Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) through (4), where teachers and staff, etc. come to fall under an on-duty disaster due to an act of self-harm, on-duty medical care benefits shall not be paid; provided, where such act of self-harm was committed in a state in which normal cognitive capacity, etc. was distinctly impaired for reasons related to the performance of duties, and where any of the following grounds apply, on-duty medical care benefits shall be paid: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Where teachers and staff, etc. who have received or are receiving medical care for a mental illness arising in the course of performing duties or in relation to duties committed an act of self-harm in a mentally abnormal state;
  2. Where teachers and staff, etc. who are receiving medical care for an on-duty injury or disease committed an act of self-harm in a mentally abnormal state caused by such on-duty injury or disease;
  3. Where a substantial causal relationship is recognized between the act of self-harm and a mentally abnormal state arising in the course of performing duties or in relation to duties.
  (6) In making a determination regarding an on-duty disease, consideration shall be given to the characteristics of the duties of teachers and staff, etc., gender, age, constitution, usual health condition, existence of pre-existing diseases, sick leave, leave of absence, and retirement.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 29-2 (Medical consultation on medical care) The TP may seek consultation from medical professionals on the following matters:
  1. The appropriateness of on-duty medical care benefits;
  2. The appropriateness of decisions on the period of medical care pursuant to Article 30 and decisions on extension of the period of medical care pursuant to Article 31;
  3. The appropriateness of rehabilitation benefits pursuant to Articles 26 and 27 of the Act on accident compensation as applied and disability benefits pursuant to Article 28 of the same Act;
  4. The appropriateness of nursing care benefits pursuant to Article 33-2 of the Act;
  5. Other matters that the TP deems to require specialized medical consultation in relation to medical care and re-treatment, etc.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 30 (Approval of on-duty medical care) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. intend to receive medical care at a medical care institution with on-duty medical care benefits (including re-treatment for which on-duty medical care benefits are provided; hereinafter referred to as "on-duty medical care"), the relevant teachers and staff, etc. shall submit an application for approval of on-duty medical care, together with a medical certificate clearly stating the period of medical care (limited to one issued by a medical care institution), to the head of the affiliated school institution; provided, where prior approval cannot be obtained due to the need for emergency treatment for an injury or disease, an application for approval shall be filed without delay after the commencement of such medical care.
  (2) Where the head of a school institution receives an application pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall, after investigating the circumstances of the injury or disease, attach the following documents to the application and forward them to the TP within 7 days:
  1. A copy of the notice of health examination results;
  2. A report on the investigation of the circumstances of the injury or disease.
  (3) Where the TP receives an application and related documents pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall determine whether to approve on-duty medical care and the period of such medical care, and shall send a written decision to the applicant, the head of the school institution, and the person entrusted with duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 30-2 Deleted. <Sep. 18, 2018>

Article 31 (Extension of the period of on-duty medical care) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. intend to receive medical care beyond the period of on-duty medical care determined pursuant to Article 30(3), or intend to extend the period of on-duty medical care beyond an actual medical care period of 3 years pursuant to the proviso of Article 22(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, they shall submit an application for approval of extension of the period of on-duty medical care to the TP, attaching a medical certificate (limited to one issued by a medical care institution and containing a doctor's opinion on the details of the required on-duty medical care, the necessity of extending the period of on-duty medical care, and the required period of on-duty medical care).
  (2) Where the TP receives an application for approval of extension of the period of on-duty medical care pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall decide whether to approve the extension of the period of on-duty medical care and the period of on-duty medical care (limited to cases where an extension is approved), and shall send the written decision to the applicant and to any person entrusted with duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32 (Claim for and payment of costs of on-duty medical care benefits) (1) Where a medical care institution provides on-duty medical care, it shall claim the costs of on-duty medical care benefits calculated pursuant to Article 25 of the Act on accident compensation as applied by attaching a statement of details to the medical cost claim form and submitting it to the TP; provided, where the TP has entrusted duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree, the claim shall be submitted to the entrusted party.
  (2) Where the TP or a person entrusted with duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act receives a claim for the costs of on-duty medical care benefits under paragraph (1), it shall examine the details of the claim and pay the costs to the medical care institution; provided, the costs of on-duty medical care benefits falling under any of the following subparagraphs may be paid directly to the beneficiary:
  1. Among the costs of medical care benefits under Article 25(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the portion of medical costs paid by the beneficiary to the medical care institution pursuant to Article 44 of the National Health Insurance Act;
  2. The costs of medical care benefits under subparagraphs 2 and 3 of Article 25 of the Act on accident compensation as applied and Article 32-2 of this Decree.
  (3) A person who intends to receive direct payment of the costs of on-duty medical care benefits falling under paragraph (2) 2 pursuant to the proviso of paragraph (2) shall claim such costs from the TP by submitting a claim for the costs of on-duty medical care benefits, with a statement of details, receipts, and a medical certificate issued by a medical care institution attached thereto.
  (4) Where a person entrusted with duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act has paid the costs of on-duty medical care benefits under paragraph (2), that person shall submit the claim for benefit costs to the TP with a statement of details attached thereto, and the TP shall examine the claim and pay the costs within 1 month.
  (5) Where the TP deems it necessary to urgently pay the costs of on-duty medical care benefits because it is evident that teachers and staff, etc. sustained injuries in the course of performing their duties, the TP may take measures necessary for on-duty medical care, such as notifying a medical care institution of its intention to pay the costs of on-duty medical care benefits and the scope of such payment, even prior to approval of on-duty medical care under Article 30.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32-2 (Calculation of costs of on-duty medical care benefits) "Medical care benefit costs prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 25 (3) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means the following medical care benefit costs:
  1. Where normal treatment is difficult through medical care under Article 25(1)1 or 2 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, or where normal social life is difficult after treatment and separate medical care is required, the costs of medicines, medical treatment, medical procedures (including plastic surgery), equipment, rehabilitation treatment, etc. necessary therefor, as determined by the TP;
  2. Among the costs exceeding the fee schedule for payment of medical care benefit costs under Article 25(1)1 or 2 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the medical care benefit costs determined by the TP.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32-3 (Requirements and procedures for re-treatment) (1) A person who has received on-duty medical care benefits may apply to the TP for re-treatment pursuant to Article 33-3 of the Act where all of the following requirements are met; provided, where a lump-sum disability compensation has been received pursuant to Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, re-treatment may not be applied for until 5 years have elapsed from the date of such payment:
  1. There shall be a substantial causal relationship between the healed on-duty injury or disease and the injury or disease subject to re-treatment;
  2. There shall be a need for active treatment, such as surgery (including surgery to remove internal fixation devices such as metal pins inserted by internal fixation and reoperation of the amputation site for fitting a prosthetic hand or prosthetic leg), for the condition of the injury or disease subject to re-treatment, and it shall be recognized that medical treatment effects can be medically expected.
  (2) Where teachers and staff, etc. intend to receive re-treatment pursuant to paragraph (1), they shall submit an application for approval of on-duty re-treatment to the TP, attaching the documents set forth in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. A medical certificate (limited to one issued by a medical care institution that contains a doctor's opinion on the details of the required re-treatment and the required period of medical care);
  2. Copies of medical records related to the medical care;
  3. Other copies of medical records that can substantiate the grounds for re-treatment.
  (3) Where the TP receives an application for re-treatment pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall decide whether to approve the re-treatment and the period of re-treatment (limited to cases where approval of re-treatment is granted) after deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee, and shall send the written decision to the applicant and to any person entrusted with duties related to on-duty medical care benefits pursuant to Article 20 of the Act and Article 14 of this Decree.
  (4) Where the TP deems it necessary to determine whether to approve re-treatment, it may require the applicant to undergo a medical examination at a medical care institution designated by the TP. In such cases, the costs incurred for the medical examination shall be borne by the TP.
  (5) Article 31 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the extension of the period of re-treatment.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32-4 (Medical care at medical institutions other than medical care institutions) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. receive medical care (including re-treatment; hereinafter the same shall apply) at a medical institution other than a medical care institution due to urgent necessity or other unavoidable circumstances, on-duty medical care benefits may be paid only where such care is recognized by the TP.
  (2) Where teachers and staff, etc. receive medical care at a medical institution other than a medical care institution pursuant to paragraph (1), they shall apply for approval of on-duty medical care pursuant to Article 30 without delay, upon commencement of such medical care. In such cases, a written statement explaining the reasons why medical care could not be received at a medical care institution shall be attached.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32-5 (Change of medical care institutions) Where a person undergoing medical care intends to change the medical care institution, he or she shall submit a copy of the written decision approving on-duty medical care pursuant to Article 30(3) to the medical care institution to which the change is to be made.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 32-6 Deleted. <Sep. 18, 2018>

Article 32-7 (Termination of medical care) (1) Where the TP determines that no medical treatment effects can be medically expected even if continued treatment is provided for an injury or disease of a person undergoing medical care due to an on-duty injury or disease, it may terminate the medical care pursuant to the Act or this Decree after deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee.
  (2) Where the TP intends to terminate medical care pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall notify the relevant teachers and staff, etc. of such fact in advance.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 2 Nursing Benefits, Assistive Devices, and Assistive Device Allowances

Article 33 (Requirements and procedures for payment of nursing care benefits) (1) The requirements for payment of nursing care benefits pursuant to Article 33-2 of the Act shall be as prescribed in Appendix 4.
  (2) Nursing care benefits shall be paid for the days on which nursing care was actually provided to a person who satisfies the requirements for payment of nursing care benefits pursuant to paragraph (1).
  (3) With respect to the standards for payment of nursing care benefits, Article 59(3) and (4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  (4) Where a person entitled to nursing care benefits receives re-treatment pursuant to Article 33-3 of the Act, nursing care benefits shall not be paid during the period of such re-treatment.
  (5) A person who intends to receive nursing care benefits shall submit a claim for nursing care benefits to the TP, attaching the documents prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Documentary evidence of the provision of nursing care and the costs incurred therefor;
  2. A doctor's written opinion stating that nursing care is required as the person satisfies the requirements for payment of nursing care benefits pursuant to paragraph (1);
  3. A disability medical certificate for the Teachers' Pension; provided, this shall not apply where the TP exempts the submission thereof.
  (6) Where the TP receives a claim for nursing care benefits pursuant to paragraph (5), it shall examine the claim and pay the benefits.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 34 (Standards for payment of assistive devices or assistive device allowances) (1) The eligibility for and standards for payment of assistive devices pursuant to Article 33-2 of the Act shall be determined by applying mutatis mutandis the matters concerning rehabilitation assistive devices and dentures that are determined in accordance with the standards for calculation of medical care benefits pursuant to Article 40(5) of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act. <Amended on Jul. 2, 2019; Sep. 29, 2021>
  (2) A person who intends to receive an assistive device or an assistive device allowance shall submit a claim for an assistive device or an assistive device allowance to the TP, attaching the documents prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Sep. 29, 2021>
  1. Documentary evidence of the cost of the assistive device;
  2. A doctor's written opinion stating that an assistive device is required as the person falls under the eligibility for and standards for payment of assistive devices pursuant to paragraph (1).
  (3) Where the TP receives a claim for an assistive device or an assistive device allowance pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall examine the claim and pay the relevant benefits. <Amended on Sep. 29, 2021>
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]
  [Title Amended on Sep. 29, 2021.]
