Subsection 3 Rehabilitation Benefits

Article 38 Deleted. <Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 39 (Requirements and procedures for payment of rehabilitation exercise costs) (1) "Disability prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 26 (1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means any of the following disabilities: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Functional disability of at least 1 of the 3 major joints of an arm or a leg;
  2. Deformation of the spine, functional disability, or neurological disability;
  3. Disability of the muscles or nerves of an arm or a leg (including cases where a disability of an arm or a leg has occurred due to injury to the brain or spinal cord), which falls under disability grades 1 through 12 as prescribed in Appendix 5.
  (2) Teachers and staff, etc. who intend to receive rehabilitation exercise costs pursuant to Article 26 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall, after performing rehabilitation exercises at a rehabilitation exercise institution (limited to a person registered as a business operator pursuant to Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act in relation to sports activities), submit a claim for rehabilitation exercise costs to the TP, attaching the documents prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. Documentary evidence of the performance of rehabilitation exercises and the costs incurred therefor;
  2. A doctor's written opinion stating that rehabilitation exercises are required as the person falls under the disability prescribed in paragraph (1).
  (3) Where the TP receives a claim for rehabilitation exercise costs pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall examine the claim and pay the costs; provided, where the rehabilitation costs fall under medical care pursuant to any subparagraph of Article 22(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, on-duty medical care benefit costs and rehabilitation exercise costs shall not be paid in duplicate for the same medical care.
  (4) The period eligible for payment of rehabilitation exercise costs pursuant to Article 26 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall be within 3 months from the date on which the relevant teachers and staff, etc. commence rehabilitation exercises; provided, any period during which rehabilitation exercises could not be performed due to unavoidable reasons such as natural disasters or the occurrence of a large-scale infectious disease shall not be included in the eligible period. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 40 (Requirements and procedures for payment of psychological counseling costs) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. undergoing on-duty medical care intend to receive psychological counseling pursuant to Article 27 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, they shall submit an application for approval of psychological counseling to the TP in advance, attaching psychological test materials, copies of medical records related to the medical care, etc., and obtain approval.
  (2) A person who has obtained approval for psychological counseling pursuant to paragraph (1) shall, in order to receive psychological counseling costs pursuant to Article 27 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, after receiving psychological counseling at a psychological counseling institution (limited to a person registered as a business operator pursuant to Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act in relation to psychological counseling), submit a claim for psychological counseling costs to the TP, attaching documentary evidence of the provision of psychological counseling and the costs incurred therefor.
  (3) Where the TP receives a claim for psychological counseling costs pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall examine the claim and pay the costs; provided, where the psychological counseling falls under medical care pursuant to any subparagraph of Article 22(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, on-duty medical care benefit costs and psychological counseling costs shall not be paid in duplicate for the same medical care.
  (4) The period eligible for payment of psychological counseling costs pursuant to Article 27 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall be within 3 months from the date on which the person who obtained approval for psychological counseling pursuant to paragraph (1) commences psychological counseling; provided, any period during which psychological counseling could not be provided due to unavoidable reasons such as natural disasters or the occurrence of a large-scale infectious disease shall not be included in the eligible period. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (5) Psychological counseling shall commence within 1 month from the date on which notice of the approval decision is received pursuant to paragraph (1); where it does not commence within such 1-month period, the date on which 1 month has elapsed from the date of receipt of the notice of the approval decision shall be deemed the date on which psychological counseling commenced. <Added on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 4 Disability Benefits

Article 41 (Determination of disability grades) (1) "The grades according to the degree of disability prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied means the grades according to the degree of disability as prescribed in Appendix 5 (hereinafter referred to as "disability grades").
  (2) Where a disability not prescribed in Appendix 5 exists, the disability grade shall be determined by reference to the disability grade corresponding to a similar disability.
  (3) Where 2 or more disabilities corresponding to disability grades exist pursuant to Article 31 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the disability grade shall be determined as the disability grade corresponding to the most severe disability; provided, where 2 or more disabilities corresponding to grades 2 through 13 exist, disability grades by body part shall first be determined for the 2 most severe disabilities in accordance with Appendix 5, and a composite disability grade shall then be determined in accordance with Appendix 6.
  (4) Matters necessary for determining disability grades other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be prescribed by the TP.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 14, 2025]

Article 42 (Claim for disability benefits) (1) A person who intends to receive a disability pension or a disability lump-sum benefit pursuant to Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit a claim for disability benefits, attaching a disability medical certificate for the Teachers' Pension issued by a medical care institution, to the head of the relevant school institution.
  (2) Where the head of a school institution receives a claim for disability benefits, etc. pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall, without delay, investigate and verify the circumstances of the disability and shall send the claim, etc. to the TP, attaching the documents prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. A copy of the notice of health examination results;
  2. An investigation report on the circumstances of the disability.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 43 (Report of loss of entitlement to disability pension) Where a person entitled to receive a disability pension pursuant to Article 28 of the Act on accident compensation as applied (hereinafter referred to as a "disability pension beneficiary") dies, the person obligated to report the death pursuant to Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations shall report such fact to the TP within 30 days from the date of death.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 44 (Redetermination of disability grades upon claim) (1) Where a beneficiary of a disability pension experiences a deterioration or improvement in the degree of disability, he or she shall submit to the TP a claim for redetermination of the disability grade pursuant to Article 30(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, together with a disability diagnosis certificate for the Teachers' Pension issued by a medical care institution.
  (2) Where the TP receives a claim for redetermination of the disability grade, etc. pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall send to the claimant a written decision specifying the following matters, after deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee:
  1. Whether the disability grade is to be redetermined;
  2. Where the disability grade is to be redetermined, the disability grade so redetermined.
  (3) Where the TP deems it necessary in order to determine the matters under the subparagraphs of paragraph (2), it may require the beneficiary of a disability pension to undergo a diagnosis at a medical care institution designated by the TP. In this case, the costs incurred for the diagnosis shall be borne by the TP.
  (4) A disability grade redetermined pursuant to paragraph (2) shall apply from the month following the month in which the date of diagnosis stated in the disability diagnosis certificate for the Teachers' Pension under paragraph (1) falls.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 45 (Redetermination of disability grade ex officio) (1) With respect to a beneficiary of a disability pension who falls under any of the following subparagraphs (excluding cases in which, even if the disability grade corresponding to the disability under the following subparagraphs is changed, the final disability grade remains unchanged because the grade of another disability is Grade 1; hereinafter referred to as a "person subject to redetermination of disability grade"), the TP shall conduct a redetermination of the disability grade within 1 year from the date on which 2 years have elapsed from the date on which the decision on payment of the disability pension was made; in such cases, the redetermination of the disability grade shall be conducted only once: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Where, among disabilities eligible for payment of a disability pension, there is 1 or more disabilities falling under Grade 1(3), Grade 2(3), Grade 3(3), Grade 5(2), Grade 7(4), Grade 9(10), or Grade 12(15) as prescribed in Appendix 5;
  2. Where, among disabilities eligible for payment of a disability pension, there is 1 or more disabilities falling under Grade 6 (5), Grade 7 (14), Grade 8 (2), Grade 9 (17), Grade 10 (14), Grade 11 (12), or Grade 12 (16) as prescribed in Appendix 5 (limited to cases where the disability grade has been determined based on spinal nerve root disability);
  3. Where, among disabilities eligible for payment of a disability pension, there is 1 or more disabilities falling under Grade 1(6) or (8), Grade 4(6), Grade 5(6) or (7), Grade 6(6) or (7), Grade 7(7) or (11), Grade 8(4), (6), or (7), Grade 9(13) or (15), Grade 10(9), (12), or (13), Grade 11(9) or (10), Grade 12(9), (10), (12), or (14), or Grade 13(8) or (11) as prescribed in Appendix 5 (limited to cases where the disability grade has been determined based on the motor function of bodily joints);
  4. Where, among disabilities eligible for payment of a disability pension, there exists a disability not prescribed in the disability grades prescribed in Appendix 5, and there are 1 or more disabilities falling under any of subparagraphs 1 through 3.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a person subject to disability grade redetermination undergoes re-treatment, the TP shall conduct a single redetermination of the disability grade within 1 year from the date on which 2 years have elapsed from the date of cure after such re-treatment (where the disability grade has been changed, from the date on which the payment decision for the corresponding disability pension is made).
  (3) Where the TP intends to conduct a redetermination of a disability grade pursuant to paragraph (1) or (2), the TP shall require the relevant person subject to disability grade redetermination to undergo a diagnosis at a medical care institution designated by the TP; in such cases, the cost incurred for such diagnosis shall be borne by the TP.
  (4) Where the TP intends to require a diagnosis pursuant to the former part of paragraph (3), the TP shall notify the relevant person subject to disability grade redetermination of the commencement date of the redetermination, the deadline for diagnosis, the medical care institutions at which the diagnosis may be conducted, and other matters necessary for the redetermination.
  (5) A person who has undergone a diagnosis pursuant to the former part of paragraph (3) shall submit to the TP a disability diagnosis certificate for the Teachers' Pension by the medical care institution that conducted the diagnosis, within 6 months from the commencement date of the redetermination. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (6) Where the TP receives a disability diagnosis certificate pursuant to paragraph (5), the TP shall send to the relevant person subject to disability grade redetermination a written decision specifying the following matters, after deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee:
  1. Whether the disability grade is to be redetermined;
  2. Where the disability grade is redetermined, the disability grade so determined.
  (7) The disability grade redetermined pursuant to paragraph (6) shall apply from the month following the month in which the date of diagnosis pursuant to paragraph (3) falls.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46 (Disability status of beneficiaries of disability pension) The "degree of disability status prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 30(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means a disability status corresponding to disability grades 1 through 14 as prescribed in Article 41 of this Decree and Appendices 5 and 6.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46-2 (Request for diagnosis to confirm disability status) (1) The TP may require the relevant person to undergo a diagnosis at a medical care institution designated by the TP in order to confirm whether the person falls under the degree of disability status prescribed in this Decree and whether the degree of disability has worsened or improved, pursuant to Article 30(1) and (2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (2) Where a diagnosis is required pursuant to paragraph (1), matters concerning the diagnostic procedure and the redetermination of disability grades based on the diagnostic results, etc. shall apply mutatis mutandis to Article 45 (3) through (7). <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46-3 (Payment of disability benefits to a person whose whereabouts are unknown) (1) A person who is to become an heir (who must fall within the scope of survivors prescribed in Article 2(1)2 of the Act; hereafter the same shall apply in this paragraph) and who intends to receive disability benefits pursuant to Article 33(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit a disability benefit claim to the TP, attaching the following documents:
  1. Documents proving that the person is to become an heir;
  2. Where a representative among persons who are to become heirs of the same rank files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the persons who are to become heirs;
  3. Documents proving the fact that the person entitled to receive disability benefits has been missing for at least 1 year (referring to documents confirmed by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or the chief of a police station).
  (2) The "interest prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 33(3) and the latter part of Article 33(4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means, respectively, interest calculated by applying the highest rate among the time deposit interest rates applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of the relevant year.
  (3) A person who intends to receive the amount corresponding to the difference in benefit amount and the interest pursuant to the latter part of Article 33(4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit a claim for the difference in disability pension benefits to the TP.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 4-2 Survivors' Benefits for Occupational Accidents

Article 46-4 (Claim for disability survivors' pension) A person who intends to receive disability survivors' pension pursuant to Article 35 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit a claim for disability survivors' pension to the TP, attaching the following documents:
  1. Documents proving the death of the beneficiary of a disability pension and that the claimant is a survivor of the deceased;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the survivors pursuant to Article 23;
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46-5 (Claim for on-duty survivors' pension) (1) A person who intends to receive on-duty survivors' pension or on-duty survivors' compensation (hereinafter referred to as "on-duty survivors' benefits") pursuant to Articles 36 and 37 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit a claim for on-duty survivors' benefits to the head of the school institution to which the teachers and staff, etc. belonged, together with the following documents:
  1. Documents proving the death of teachers and staff, etc. and that the claimant is a survivor of the deceased;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the survivors pursuant to Article 23;
  (2) Upon receipt of a claim under paragraph (1), the head of the school institution shall, without delay, investigate and verify the circumstances of death and shall forward the claim to the TP, attaching a report on the investigation of the circumstances of death.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46-6 (Report on loss of entitlement to disability survivors' pension) Where a person entitled to receive disability survivors' pension or on-duty survivors' pension loses such entitlement pursuant to Article 40(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the person classified under the following subparagraphs shall report the fact to the TP within 30 days from the date on which the relevant ground arises:
  1. Where a person entitled to receive a disability survivors' pension or an on-duty survivors' pension dies: The person obligated to report the death pursuant to Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations;
  2. Where the person remarries or the kinship relationship with the deceased teachers and staff is terminated: The person concerned;
  3. Where a child or grandchild reaches 19 years of age: The person concerned or the former legal representative;
  4. Where the disability status of a child or grandchild aged 19 or older who was in a disability status is resolved: The person concerned, the legal representative, or the former legal representative.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 46-7 (Application for transfer of entitlement to disability survivors' pension) Where a person entitled to receive disability survivors' pension or on-duty survivors' pension loses such entitlement or has been missing for at least 1 year and, pursuant to Article 40(2) or Article 41 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, a survivor of the same order of priority or of the next order of priority seeks to receive the disability survivors' pension or the on-duty survivors' pension, the relevant survivor shall submit to the TP an application for transfer of entitlement to the disability survivors' pension or the on-duty survivors' pension, together with the following documents: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Documents certifying that the applicant is a survivor of a disability pension beneficiary or a survivor of a teacher or staff member who died on duty;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the survivors pursuant to Article 23;
  3. Documents according to the following categories:
  a. Where the case falls under Article 40(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied: Documents according to the following categories:
  1) Where the case involves death, remarriage, termination of the kinship relationship with the deceased teacher or staff member, or where a child or grandchild who is not in a disability status has reached 19 years of age: A certificate concerning family relation records or a resident registration certificate;
  2) Where the disability status of a child or grandchild aged 19 or older who had been in a disability status has been resolved: Documents certifying the degree of disability, such as a certificate of registration as a person with a disability pursuant to Article 32 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities, or documents certifying the cancellation of such registration pursuant to Article 32-3 of the same Act.
  b. Where the case falls under Article 41 of the Act on accident compensation as applied: Documents certifying, by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or the chief of a police station, that the disability pension beneficiary has been missing for at least 1 year.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 5 Relief Benefits

Article 47 (Disaster relief grant) (1) The scope of damage caused by a disaster under Article 42(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means damage suffered by a house owned by a teacher or staff member or his or her spouse (including a share in a multi-unit housing; hereafter the same shall apply), or a house in which the teacher or staff member customarily resides that is owned by a lineal ascendant or descendant of the teacher or staff member or of his or her spouse, as a result of fire, flood, heavy rain, heavy snowfall, storm, tidal wave, or natural or man-made phenomena equivalent thereto.
  (2) The amount of a relief grant by degree of damage caused by a disaster under Article 42(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall be as follows:
  1. Where a house is completely destroyed, lost, or demolished: 3.9 times the average amount of the standard monthly income of all public officials;
  2. Where at least 1/2 of a house is destroyed, lost, or demolished (excluding cases falling under subparagraph 1): 2.6 times the average amount of the standard monthly income of all public officials;
  3. Where at least 1/3 of a house is destroyed, lost, or demolished (excluding cases falling under subparagraphs 1 and 2): 1.3 times the average amount of the standard monthly income of all public officials.
  (3) A person who intends to receive a disaster relief grant pursuant to Article 42 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit an application for a disaster relief grant to the TP, attaching a certificate confirming the damage status issued by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or the chief of a fire station; in such cases, the TP shall verify the following administrative information through the joint use of administrative information pursuant to Article 36 (1) or (2) of the Electronic Government Act, and if the applicant does not consent to verification of the information under subparagraph 1, the applicant shall be required to submit the relevant documents directly: <Amended on May 12, 2020>
  1. A copy of the resident registration certificate;
  2. A copy of the building register.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 47-2 (Condolence grant upon death) (1) "One teacher or staff member prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the latter part of Article 43(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied means the teacher or staff member with the highest priority ranking among those in the following order of priority:
  1. The teacher or staff member who is the spouse of the deceased person;
  2. The oldest teacher or staff member among the closest lineal descendants of the deceased person;
  3. The oldest teacher or staff member among the spouses of the closest lineal descendants of the deceased person;
  4. The oldest teacher or staff member among the parents of the deceased person.
  (2) Where the deceased teacher or staff member has no spouse pursuant to Article 43(2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the condolence grant upon death shall be paid to the person who conducted the funeral and performs ancestral rites, who ranks highest in priority among the following persons; provided, among the persons who conducted the funeral and perform ancestral rites, where there is a teacher or staff member who is a lineal descendant of the deceased teacher or staff member, the condolence grant upon death shall be paid to such lineal descendant teacher or staff member, notwithstanding subparagraph 1:
  1. The oldest person among the closest lineal descendants of the deceased teacher or staff member;
  2. The oldest person among the closest lineal ascendants of the deceased teacher or staff member;
  3. The oldest person among the siblings of the deceased teacher or staff member.
  (3) A person who intends to receive a condolence grant upon death pursuant to Article 43 of the Act on accident compensation as applied shall submit an application for a condolence grant upon death to the TP together with the documents listed in the following subparagraphs; provided, where the grant is to be paid to the teacher or staff member who had supported the deceased pursuant to the latter part of Article 43(1) of the Act on accident compensation as applied, the TP may verify a resident registration certificate through the joint use of administrative information pursuant to Article 36(1) and (2) of the Electronic Government Act, and where the applicant does not consent to such verification, the applicant shall be required to submit the relevant document directly: <Amended on May 12, 2020>
  1. Documents capable of proving the fact of death of the spouse, etc. of a teacher or staff member pursuant to Article 43(1) and (2) of the Act on accident compensation as applied;
  2. Documents proving the relationship with the deceased referred to in subparagraph 1.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 2 Retirement Benefits and Retirement Survivors' Benefits

Article 52-3 (Confirmation of retirement due to revision or abolition of organizational structure and authorized strength) (1) Where a teacher or staff member affiliated with a school institution retires because his or her position is abolished or the number of personnel exceeds the authorized strength as a result of the revision or abolition of the organizational structure and authorized strength or a reduction in the budget, pursuant to Article 43(1) 4 of the Act on pension as applied, the head of the relevant school institution shall submit to the TP materials by which the relevant reason, the authorized strength, and the actual number of personnel may be confirmed.
  (2) Where the TP receives the materials pursuant to paragraph (1), it shall verify whether the retirement of the teacher or staff member falls under retirement pursuant to Article 43(1) 4 of the Act on pension as applied and shall send a written confirmation thereof to the head of the relevant school institution.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]
  [Title Amended on Jul. 2, 2019.]

Article 52-4 (Disability status for receipt of retirement pension) "Disability status prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 43(1) 5 and Article 44 of the Act on pension as applied means a case falling under disability grades 1 through 7 pursuant to Article 41 of this Decree and Appendices 5 and 6.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 52-5 (Report of loss of entitlement to retirement pension or early retirement pension) Where a beneficiary of a retirement pension pursuant to Article 43(1) of the Act on pension as applied or a beneficiary of an early retirement pension pursuant to Article 43(2) of the same Act dies, the person obligated to report the death pursuant to Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations shall report such fact to the TP within 30 days from the date of death.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 52-6 (Standards for recognition of substantive period of marriage) (1) In calculating the substantive period of marriage pursuant to Article 45(1) of the Act on pension as applied, any period falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be excluded from the period of marriage:
  1. A period of disappearance pursuant to Article 27(1) of the Civil Act;
  2. A period during which a person is registered as having an unknown residence pursuant to Article 20(6) of the Resident Registration Act.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where any of the following periods exists, the relevant period shall apply:
  1. A period agreed between the parties to a divorce during which no substantive marital relationship existed;
  2. A period recognized by a court judgment or other judicial decision as a period during which no substantive marital relationship existed.
  (3) A person entitled to retirement benefits under Article 28(1) 1 of the Act mutatis mutandis, a person entitled to a divided pension under Article 45(1) of the same Act, or a person who has claimed an installment of a lump-sum retirement pension, etc. under Article 49(1) of the same Act shall report the relevant details to the TP where there exists any period prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2) of this Article.
  (4) Matters necessary for the procedures and methods for reporting under paragraph (3) shall be determined by the TP.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 52-7 (Procedures for claiming installment pension) (1) A person who intends to claim installment pension pursuant to Article 45(3) of the Act on pension as applied (including cases where a claim is made for installment payment of lump-sum retirement pension, etc. pursuant to Article 49 of the same Act) or to file an advance claim for installment pension pursuant to Article 48(1) of the same Act shall submit an application for claiming installment pension, etc. together with the following documents to the TP; provided, in cases involving a person who was in a de facto marital relationship, documents proving such fact shall be submitted together with the application for claiming installment pension, etc. to the TP:
  1. A copy of a certificate of family relations;
  2. A copy of a certificate of marriage relations;
  3. A copy each of a resident registration transcript and a resident registration abstract.
  (2) Installment pension pursuant to Article 45(1) of the Act on pension as applied shall be paid from the month following the month in which the grounds for payment arise through the month in which the grounds for payment of the installment pension cease to exist.
  (3) A person who intends to cancel an advance claim for installment pension pursuant to Article 48(3) of the Act on pension as applied shall submit an application for cancellation of the advance claim for installment pension to the TP, attaching a copy of an identification card such as a resident registration card.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 53 (Claim for retirement benefits) (1) A person who intends to receive retirement pension, early retirement pension, lump-sum retirement pension, lump-sum retirement pension contribution, or lump-sum retirement benefits pursuant to Articles 43 and 51 of the Act on pension as applied shall submit a claim for retirement benefits to the TP. <Amended on May 12, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a person who intends to claim lump-sum retirement benefits falls under the criteria prescribed by the TP due to a short period of service or a small amount, such person may claim the lump-sum retirement benefit by telephone without submitting a claim for retirement benefits. In such cases, the TP shall conduct verification procedures such as audio recording for the purpose of verifying the identity of the claimant and the fact of the claim. <Added on Jan. 14, 2025>
  (3) Where a person retires due to reasons such as the amendment or abolition of the organizational structure and authorized strength pursuant to Article 43(1) 4 of the Act on pension as applied and claims a retirement pension, such person shall attach the confirmation issued by the TP pursuant to Article 52-3(2) of this Decree to the claim for retirement benefits under paragraph (1). <Amended on Jul. 2, 2019>
  (4) Where a person claims a retirement pension on the grounds that the person falls under a disability status pursuant to Article 43(1) 5 of the Act on Pension as Applied and Article 52-4 of this Decree, the person shall attach a disability medical certificate for the Teachers' Pension issued by a medical care institution that is proving the disability status to the claim for retirement benefits under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 53-2 (Mandatory retirement age or maximum age for service) The mandatory retirement age or maximum age for service pursuant to Article 42 (4) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. Teachers: The mandatory retirement age applicable to educational public officials pursuant to Article 47 of Educational Public Officials Act;
  2. Administrative staff: The mandatory retirement age applicable to public officials in general service pursuant to Article 74 of State Public Officials Act.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 54 (Special cases for calculation and payment of retirement benefits) Where the TP pays lump-sum retirement pension, lump-sum retirement benefit, lump-sum retirement survivors' pension, or a retirement survivors' lump sum to a person who was appointed again as a teacher or staff member after having retired as a teacher or staff member, a public official, or having been discharged from military service and who received aggregation of the period of service pursuant to Article 32(1) of the Act, upon his or her retirement or death, and where the amount of benefits calculated on the basis of the aggregated period of service is less than the sum of the amounts prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs, the TP shall calculate and pay the relevant benefits in the amount equal to the sum of the amounts prescribed in each of the following subparagraphs:
  1. The refund amount pursuant to Article 32(2) of the Act and interest thereon (referring to interest calculated on a compound annual basis by applying, for each year, the highest rate among the fixed deposit interest rates applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of the relevant year, after the refund amount has been paid);
  2. Lump-sum retirement pension, lump-sum retirement benefit, lump-sum retirement survivors' pension, or retirement survivors' lump sum calculated on the basis of the period of service served after being reappointed as a teacher or staff member.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 54-2 (Payment of retirement benefits for missing persons) (1) Where a person who is to become an heir of a person entitled to receive retirement benefits (who shall fall within the scope of survivors under Article 2(1) 2 of the Act; hereafter the same shall apply in this paragraph) intends to receive retirement benefits pursuant to Article 52(1) of the Act on pension as applied, he or she shall submit a claim for retirement benefits to the TP, attaching the following documents:
  1. Documents proving that the person is to become an heir;
  2. Where a representative among persons who are to become heirs of the same rank files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the persons who are to become heirs;
  3. Documents proving that the person entitled to receive retirement benefits has been missing for at least 1 year (referring to documents confirmed by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or the chief of a police station).
  (2) "Interest prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 52(3) and the latter part of Article 52(4) of the Act on pension as applied means interest calculated by applying the highest rate among fixed deposit interest rates applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each relevant year.
  (3) A person who intends to receive the amount corresponding to the difference in benefit amount and interest pursuant to the latter part of Article 52(4) of the Act on pension as applied shall submit a claim for the difference in retirement benefit payments to the TP.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 54-3 (Claim for retirement survivors' pension, retirement survivors' pension additional amount, retirement survivors' pension special additional amount, lump-sum retirement survivors' pension, and retirement survivors' lump sum) (1) A person who intends to receive retirement survivors' pension, retirement survivors' pension additional amount, retirement survivors' pension special additional amount, lump-sum retirement survivors' pension, or retirement survivors' lump sum pursuant to Articles 54, 55, and 58 of the Act on pension as applied shall submit a claim for retirement survivors' benefits to the TP with the following documents attached: <Amended on May 12, 2020>
  1. Documents proving the death of a person entitled to receive retirement pension or early retirement pension and proving that the claimant is a survivor of the deceased;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the survivors pursuant to Article 23;
  3. Where the beneficiary of survivors' pension falls under Article 41(2) of the Act on pension as applied, documents proving that the beneficiary is receiving discharged service pension, retirement pension, or early retirement pension.
  (2) Deleted. <May 12, 2020>
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 54-4 (Application for transfer of entitlement to retirement survivors' pension) Where a beneficiary of a retirement survivors' pension has been missing for at least 1 year or has lost his or her entitlement, and a survivor of the same order or the next order intends to receive the retirement survivors' pension pursuant to Article 56 or Article 57(2) of the Act on pension as applied, the relevant survivor shall submit an application for transfer of entitlement to retirement survivors' pension to the TP with the following documents attached: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  1. Documents proving that the applicant is a survivor of a person entitled to receive retirement pension or early retirement pension;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the claim, documents proving that the claimant is the representative of the survivors pursuant to Article 23;
  3. Documents according to the following categories:
  a. In cases falling under Article 56 of the Act on pension as applied: Documents verified by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu or the chief of a police station confirming that the beneficiary of retirement survivors' pension has been missing for at least 1 year;
  b. In cases falling under Article 57(2) of the Act on pension as applied: Documents according to the following classifications:
  1) Where the case involves death, remarriage, termination of the kinship relationship with the deceased teacher or staff member, or where a child or grandchild who is not in a disability status has reached 19 years of age: A certificate concerning family relation records or a resident registration certificate;
  2) Where the disability status of a child or grandchild aged 19 or older who had been in a disability status has been resolved: Documents certifying the degree of disability, such as a certificate of registration as a person with a disability pursuant to Article 32 of the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities, or documents certifying the cancellation of such registration pursuant to Article 32-3 of the same Act.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 54-5 (Report on loss of entitlement to a retirement survivors' pension) Where a person entitled to receive retirement survivors' pension loses such entitlement pursuant to Article 57(1) of the Act on pension as applied, the person specified under each of the following subparagraphs shall report such fact to the TP within 30 days from the date on which the cause for the loss of entitlement occurs:
  1. Where the beneficiary of a retirement survivors' pension dies: The person obligated to report the death pursuant to Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations;
  2. Where the beneficiary remarries or where the kinship relationship otherwise terminates: The person concerned;
  3. Where a child or grandchild reaches 19 years of age: The person concerned or the former legal representative;
  4. Where the disability status of a child or grandchild aged 19 or older who was in a disability status is resolved: The person concerned, the legal representative, or the former legal representative.
  [This Article Added on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 3 Off-duty Disability Benefits

Article 55 (Claim for off-duty disability benefits) A person who intends to receive off-duty disability pension or off-duty disability lump sum pursuant to Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied shall submit a claim for disability benefits to the TP, attaching the following documents:

  2. A statement of the circumstances of the disability.

Article 56 (Determination of grades according to degree of disability) With respect to the determination and revision of grades according to the degree of disability, the disability status for maintaining entitlement to pension, and requirements for diagnosis, for a person who is to receive off-duty disability benefits pursuant to Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied, Articles 41,44 through 46, Article 46-2, Appendix 5, and Appendix 6 shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 57 (Report on loss of entitlement to off-duty disability pension) Where a recipient of an off-duty disability pension pursuant to Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied dies, the person obligated to report the death under Article 85 of the Act on Registration of Family Relations shall report such fact to the TP within 30 days from the date of death.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Subsection 5 Retirement Allowance

Article 63-2 (Claim for retirement allowance) (1) A person who intends to receive retirement allowance pursuant to Article 62(1) of the Act on pension as applied shall submit a claim for retirement allowance to the TP. <Amended on May 12, 2020>
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), where a person whose period of service is short or the amount is small falls under the standards prescribed by the TP and intends to claim retirement allowance, the person may claim the retirement allowance by telephone without submitting a claim for retirement allowance. In such case, the TP shall conduct verification procedures such as audio recording for the purpose of verifying the identity of the claimant and the fact of the claim. <Added on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 63-3 (Retirement allowance) (1) The "ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the calculation formula under Article 62(2) of the Act on pension as applied means the ratio corresponding to each of the following categories:
  1. Where the period of service is 1 year or more but less than 5 years: 6.5 percent;
  2. Where the period of service is 5 years or more but less than 10 years: 22.75 percent;
  3. Where the period of service is 10 years or more but less than 15 years: 29.25 percent;
  4. Where the period of service is 15 years or more but less than 20 years: 32.5 percent;
  5. Where the period of service is 20 years or more: 39 percent.
  (2) Where retirement allowance is calculated pursuant to Article 62(2) of the Act on pension as applied, the period of service shall not exceed 33 years.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

SECTION 4 Restriction on Benefits

Article 64 (Reduction of benefits due to gross negligence) Where teachers and staff, etc. fall under Article 44(3) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 63(3) of the Act on pension as applied disability benefits under Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied on-duty survivors' benefits or off-duty disability benefits under Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied shall be paid after deducting 1/2 of the amount of the relevant benefits. In such cases, where the benefits are pension benefits, this shall apply from the month following the month in which the relevant cause occurred. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 64-2 (Reduction of retirement survivors' benefits and survivors' benefits for occupational accidents due to failure to fulfill child-rearing responsibilities) (1) In determining whether teachers and staff, etc. have failed to fulfill child-rearing responsibilities pursuant to Article 44(4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 63(4) of the Act on pension as applied the matters prescribed in Appendix 7 shall be taken into consideration.
  (2) Where the survivors of teachers and staff, etc. intend to apply for a restriction on benefits with respect to a person who has failed to fulfill child-rearing responsibilities toward teachers and staff, etc. pursuant to Article 44(4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 63(4) of the Act on pension as applied (hereinafter in this Article referred to as a "person subject to examination for benefit restriction"), such survivors shall file an application for benefit restriction with the TP attaching the following documents:
  1. Documents proving that the applicant is a survivor of the teachers and staff, etc.;
  2. Where a representative among survivors of the same order files the application documents proving that such person is the representative of the survivors;
  3. Documents proving the failure of the person subject to examination for benefit restriction to fulfill child-rearing responsibilities.
  (3) Where the TP receives an application under paragraph (2), it shall notify the person subject to examination for benefit restriction of such fact and receive from that person documents proving the fulfillment of child-rearing responsibilities and shall verify and investigate the relevant facts.
  (4) Where the TP has verified and investigated the relevant facts pursuant to paragraph (3), it shall determine whether to restrict benefits and the rate of reduction and shall notify the applicant and the person subject to examination for benefit restriction of the results.
  (5) Notwithstanding paragraph (4), where the person subject to examination for benefit restriction has received a decision to restrict either survivors' benefits for occupational accidents or retirement survivors' benefits pursuant to Article 44(4) of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 63(4) of the Act on pension as applied, the TP may determine whether to restrict the remaining benefits and the rate of reduction without deliberation by the Benefit Examination Committee.
  (6) The TP shall calculate and pay benefits to the person subject to examination for benefit restriction in accordance with the decisions under paragraphs (4) and (5). In such cases, the reduced portion of benefits not paid to the person subject to examination for benefit restriction shall be paid as follows:
  1. Where there is a survivor of the same order as the person subject to examination for benefit restriction: Where there is 1 survivor of the same order, the full amount shall be paid to that survivor; where there are 2 or more survivors of the same order, the amount shall be divided equally and paid to them;
  2. Where there is no survivor of the same order as the person subject to examination for benefit restriction:
  a. Where benefits are fully reduced: Where there is 1 survivor of the next order, the full amount shall be paid to that survivor; where there are 2 or more survivors of the next order, the amount shall be divided equally and paid to them;
  b. Where benefits are partially reduced: It shall not be paid.
  [This Article Added on Jan. 14, 2025]

Article 65 (Reduction of benefits due to failure to undergo diagnosis) Where teachers and staff, etc. fail to undergo a diagnosis required by the TP or the head of a school institution in connection with the payment of benefits pursuant to Article 45 of the Act on accident compensation as applied or Article 64 of the Act on pension as applied within the prescribed diagnosis period without a compelling reason not to do so, 1/2 of the benefit amount shall be deducted and paid with respect to medical care benefits, disability benefits, on-duty survivors' benefits under Article 8 of the Act on accident compensation as applied, or off-duty disability benefits under Article 59 of the Act on pension as applied. In such cases, with respect to pension-type benefits, this shall apply from the month following the month in which the diagnosis period falls. <Amended on Jan. 14, 2025>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 66 (Reduction of retirement benefits and retirement allowance due to criminal punishment) (1) Where teachers and staff, etc. fall under any of the subparagraphs of Article 65(1) of the Act on pension as applied, retirement benefits and retirement allowance under the Act on pension as applied shall be paid after being reduced in accordance with the classifications in the following subparagraphs; provided, retirement pension or early retirement pension shall not be reduced until the end of the month in which the ground for reduction arises:
  1. A person falling under Article 65(1)1 or 2 of the Act on pension as applied:
  a. Retirement benefits for a person whose period of service is less than 5 years: 1/4;
  b. Retirement benefits for a person whose period of service is 5 years or more: 1/2;
  c. Retirement allowance: 1/2;
  2. A person falling under Article 65(1) 3 of the Act on pension as applied:
  a. Retirement benefits for a person whose period of service is less than 5 years: 1/8;
  b. Retirement benefits for a person whose period of service is 5 years or more: 1/4;
  c. Retirement allowance: 1/4.
  (2) With respect to the reduced amount pursuant to Article 65(2) of the Act on pension as applied, interest to be additionally paid shall be calculated by applying the highest interest rate among fixed deposit interest rates applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each relevant year, and such interest shall be included in the reduced amount on an annual compound basis for the period from the month following the month in which a portion of the retirement benefits or retirement allowance was reduced and paid until the month in which the cause for reduction ceases, and the interest accrued thereafter shall be calculated accordingly.
  (3) A person who intends to receive an amount reduced pursuant to Article 65(2) of the Act on pension as applied shall submit to the TP an application for reduced retirement benefits or an application for reduced retirement allowance, along with the documents classified as follows:
  1. Where Article 65(1)1 of the Act on pension as applied applies: A copy of a final and conclusive court judgment or a certificate of finality of a criminal judgment;
  2. Where Article 65(1)2 or 3 of the Act on pension as applied applies: A copy of a court judgment or decision, or a copy of a resolution, in cases where a disposition of impeachment or dismissal or removal by disciplinary action has been rendered null and void, revoked, or modified by a judgment or decision of a court or other authority;
  3. Other materials proving that the cause for reduction of benefits has retroactively ceased.
  (4) Where, pursuant to Article 65(3) of the Act on pension as applied, an investigation is under way or a criminal trial is pending against a teacher or staff member due to a criminal act punishable by imprisonment or heavier punishment committed for reasons arising during service (excluding cases arising from negligence unrelated to duties and cases arising from negligence occurring in the course of complying with a lawful official order of a superior), only 3/4 of the benefit amount shall be paid provisionally in the case of lump-sum retirement benefits for a person whose period of service is less than 5 years, and only 1/2 of the benefit amount shall be paid provisionally in the case of retirement allowance, and lump-sum retirement pension, lump-sum retirement pension contribution, or a lump-sum retirement benefit for a person whose period of service is 5 years or more: <Amended on Dec. 29, 2020>
  1. Deleted; <Dec. 29, 2020>
  2. Deleted; <Dec. 29, 2020>
  3. Deleted. <Dec. 29, 2020>
  (5) Pursuant to the latter part of Article 65 (3) of the Act on pension as applied, interest to be added to the remaining amount shall be calculated by applying the highest fixed-term deposit interest rate applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of that year, and such interest shall be compounded annually by adding it to the remaining amount for the period from the month following the month in which part of the retirement benefit or retirement allowance was paid until the month in which the ground for payment of the remaining amount arises, and thereafter the amount of interest shall be calculated.
  (6) The remaining amount after the priority payment pursuant to paragraph (4) shall be paid when teachers and staff, etc. whose payment has been suspended pursuant to Article 65(3) of the Act on pension as applied falls under any of the following subparagraphs; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, if an investigation procedure is recommenced with respect to the relevant case after a decision of non-referral or non-prosecution, or if prosecution is instituted and a criminal trial is pending with respect to the relevant case, such remaining amount shall not be paid: <Added on Dec. 29, 2020>
  1. When a decision of non-referral or non-prosecution is rendered;
  2. When no sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment is imposed;
  3. When a judgment of suspension of sentence for imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment is rendered and the suspension period has elapsed.
  (7) A person who intends to receive the remaining amount pursuant to the main sentence of paragraph (6) shall submit to the Corporation an application for the remaining retirement benefit or an application for the remaining retirement allowance, along with the documents classified as follows: <Amended on Jul. 14, 2020; Dec. 29, 2020>
  1. Where paragraph (6)1 applies: A decision of non-referral issued by the head of the competent police authority or a decision of non-prosecution issued by the Director of the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials or the head of the competent prosecutors' office;
  2. Where paragraph (6)2 or 3 applies: A certificate of finality of criminal judgment issued by the Director of the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials or the head of the competent prosecutors' office.
  (8) Where the head of a school institution becomes aware that a teacher or staff member belonging thereto or who formerly belonged thereto falls under Article 65 of the Act on pension as applied, he or she shall notify the TP of such fact without delay. <Amended on Dec. 29, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

  (2) "Amount prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 46(1)1 of the Act means 3,706/9,000 of the total amount of individual contributions to be borne by the teachers under Article 44(4). <Amended on Feb. 5, 2008; Jan. 1, 2010; Dec. 31, 2015>
  (3) The amount of corporate contributions under Article 47(3) of the Act shall be 5,294/9,000 of the aggregate amount of individual contributions to be borne by teachers of the relevant school pursuant to Article 44(4) of the Act. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1998; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 1, 2010; Nov. 29, 2013; Dec. 31, 2015>
  [This Article Added on Feb. 2, 1996]
  [Title Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 69 (Payment of individual contributions and corporate contributions) (1) Where the head of a school institution collects or receives individual contributions, corporate contributions, refund, or amount to be recovered, etc. and makes payment to the TP, he or she shall make such payment through a pension collection agency and shall submit a payment notice together with the paid amount. <Amended on Feb. 10, 1979; Feb. 25, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) A pension collection agency that has received the payment under paragraph (1) shall issue a receipt therefor to the head of the school institution and shall submit the payment notice to the TP. <Amended on Feb. 25, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (3) The TP shall, after examining and confirming the payment notice under paragraph (2), record it in the receipt ledger and, where there is any overpayment or underpayment, shall process a settlement thereof. <Amended on Feb. 25, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jun. 25, 1976]

Article 69-2 (Accident compensation contributions) (1) The amount of accident compensation contributions under Article 48-2(1) of the Act shall be 454/10,000 of the aggregate amount of individual contributions paid by teachers and staff, etc. excluding amounts paid due to inclusion of the period of service or retroactive aggregation. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) The accident compensation benefit reserve fund accumulated under Article 48-2(2) of the Act shall be managed by the following methods: <Amended on Dec. 31, 1985; Jun. 11, 1998; Feb. 28, 2000; Jan. 24, 2007; Jul. 29, 2008; Jan. 1, 2010>
  1. Deposits with or trusts in financial companies, etc. prescribed in each subparagraph of Article 87-2(1);
  2. Purchase of securities under Article 87-2(2) 1.
  (3) Where the accident compensation benefit reserve fund under paragraph (2) is insufficient to cover benefits under Article 48-2(3) of the Act, the amount may be temporarily borrowed from the pension fund for private school teachers and staff under Article 53-2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Fund"), and such temporary borrowing shall be repaid by the end of the following fiscal year. <Amended on Feb. 28, 2000>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Dec. 31, 1982]

Article 69-3 (Bearing of costs incurred in payment of retirement allowances) (1) Of the amount obtained by subtracting the costs listed in the following subparagraphs from the costs incurred in the payment of retirement allowance under Article 47 (3) of the Act (hereafter referred to as "costs for payment of retirement allowances" in this Article), 40/100 shall be borne by the school management entity:
  1. Costs incurred in the payment of retirement allowance to teachers and staff working at kindergartens, elementary schools, or secondary schools under Article 3 of the Act;
  2. Costs incurred in the payment of retirement allowance to administrative staff working at school foundations that establish and operate only kindergartens, elementary schools, or secondary schools under Article 3 of the Act;
  3. Costs incurred in the payment of retirement allowance to teachers and staff working at schools of not higher than the high school level among institutions subject to special cases for the scope of application under Article 60-4 of the Act;
  4. Costs incurred in the payment of retirement allowance to administrative staff working at school foundations that establish and operate only schools of not higher than the high school level among institutions subject to special cases for the scope of application under Article 60-4 of the Act.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the costs incurred in payment of retirement allowances for clinical faculty members and employees under Article 60-4(6) or (7) of the Act shall be borne in full by the school management entity. <Added on Feb. 29, 2016>
  (3) Of the costs incurred in payment of retirement allowance, the amount to be borne by the TP pursuant to the proviso of Article 47(3) of the Act shall be the amount borne by the TP as retirement allowance costs in 1992. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  (4) Of the costs incurred in payment of retirement allowances, the amount to be borne by the State pursuant to the proviso of Article 47(3) of the Act shall be the remainder after excluding the following amounts: <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  1. The amount borne by the school management entity pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2);
  2. The amount borne by the TP pursuant to paragraph (3).
  (5) Where there is no school management entity required to bear the costs of retirement allowance under paragraphs (1) and (2) due to dissolution of the corporation or other reasons, the State shall bear such costs. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  (6) In calculating the amount to be borne by a school management entity under paragraphs (1) and (2), where a retired teacher or staff belonged to 2 or more school management entities and falls under the proviso of Article 2(1)3 of the Act, the costs shall be borne by each relevant school management entity in proportion to the period of service at each entity, and where the ratios under the subparagraphs of Article 63-3 differ and a difference arises between the total amount of retirement allowance paid and the aggregate of the amounts to be borne by the respective school management entities, such difference shall be borne by the State. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  (7) The amount to be borne by a school management entity under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be paid in the month following the month in which retirement allowances are paid, based on the aggregate of the actual costs incurred on a monthly basis. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  (8) Where the amount borne by the State in the relevant year pursuant to paragraphs (4) and (5) and the latter part of paragraph (6) falls short of or exceeds the actual amount incurred, such difference shall be settled through the contribution for the following year. <Amended on Feb. 29, 2016>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Feb. 27, 2014]

Article 70 (Appropriation of national contributions) (1) The State shall appropriate in its annual budget the amount required for national contributions under Article 46 of the Act and the proviso of Article 47(3) of the Act. In such cases, where there is any shortfall from the previous year, such shortfall shall also be appropriated together. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1991; Nov. 29, 2013>
  (2) The TP shall calculate the amount required for national contributions for the following year, clearly set out the details of such calculation, and submit them to the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies (including agencies affiliated with the President and agencies and advisory bodies affiliated with the Prime Minister; hereafter the same shall apply) by March 31 of each year. <Amended on Feb. 1, 1991; Dec. 31, 1991; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 29, 2001; Jan. 24, 2007; Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 70-2 (Interest rate for settlement of national contributions) The interest accruing from the settlement of national contributions and national contribution amounts pursuant to Article 46(4) of the Act shall be calculated by applying the highest fixed-term deposit interest rate applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each relevant year and shall be settled with compound interest calculated on an annual basis for each fiscal year.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2000]

Article 71 (Payment of national contributions) (1) National contributions pursuant to Article 46 of the Act shall be divided into 4 installments per year and paid by the head of the relevant central administrative agency to the pension collection institution by January of the beginning of each installment period and the pension collection institution that receives such payment shall issue a receipt to the head of the relevant central administrative agency and transmit a notice of deposit to the TP without delay. <Amended on Feb. 1, 1991; Dec. 30, 2000; Jan. 29, 2001; Jan. 24, 2007; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2000>

Article 72 Deleted. <Feb. 25, 1984>

Article 72-2 (Collection of late payment charges) (1) Late payment charges pursuant to Article 51 of the Act shall be calculated by applying an interest rate equivalent to twice the highest fixed deposit interest rate applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of the relevant year for each year in which the overdue days and the overdue date fall; provided, where individual contributions could not be paid due to a delay in reporting appointment, an interest rate equivalent to the highest fixed deposit interest rate applied by nationwide banks as of January 1 of each year in which the relevant period falls shall be applied to the period from the first day of the month following the month in which the appointment date falls until the last day of the month preceding the month in which the report of newly appointed personnel is received by the TP. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  (2) Where contributions could not be paid within the payment deadline due to the closure of a school institution, a natural disaster, or other unavoidable reasons, late payment charges under paragraph (1) shall not be collected. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 8, 1980]

Article 73 (Compulsory collection) (1) Where amounts to be recovered under Article 25, individual contributions or corporate contributions under Article 69, or accident compensation contributions under Article 69-2 are not paid by the prescribed deadline, the TP shall issue a demand notice by setting a deadline of not less than 1 month and not more than 3 months from the payment due date. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1977; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) The demand notice under paragraph (1) shall state that, if payment is not made by the deadline specified in the demand notice, compulsory collection shall be carried out in accordance with the procedures for disposition for delinquent national taxes.
  (3) Where the TP deems compulsory collection unavoidable for any of the following reasons, it shall submit an application for approval of compulsory collection to the Minister of Education: <Added on Dec. 31, 1977; Feb. 1, 1991; Jan. 29, 2001; Feb. 24, 2003; Feb. 29, 2008; Jan. 1, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013>
  1. Where the period of delinquency has reached 6 months or more; provided, in the case of amounts to be recovered, where the demand period under paragraph (1) has elapsed;
  2. Where the school management body has been dissolved or its authorization has been revoked.
  (4) Upon receipt of an application for approval of compulsory collection under paragraph (3), the Minister of Education shall determine whether to grant approval within 30 days from the date of receipt of the application and notify the TP of the decision. <Added on Dec. 31, 1977; Feb. 1, 1991; Jan. 29, 2001; Feb. 29, 2008; Jan. 1, 2010; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (5) Where executive officers or employees of the TP carry out compulsory collection pursuant to Article 52(3) of the Act, they shall present to interested parties the approval for compulsory collection issued under paragraph (4) and their identification cards. <Added on Dec. 31, 1977; Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 73-2 (Disposition of uncollectible amounts) Disposition of uncollectible amounts under Article 52(4)3 of the Act may be made in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the whereabouts of the delinquent obligor have long been unknown or it has been confirmed that the obligor has no property;
  2. Where recovery is deemed impossible due to other unavoidable reasons.
  [This Article Added on Dec. 30, 2000]

Article 74 (Calculation of individual contributions when the standard monthly income changes) Where the standard monthly income of teachers and staff changes so that 2 or more standard monthly incomes apply within the same month the head of the relevant school institution shall calculate the individual contribution for that month on the basis of the standard monthly income as of the salary payment date of that month. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2010>
  [Title Amended on Jan. 1, 2010]

Article 75 (Reporting of changes in status) Where teachers and staff experience a change in status during service including retirement, death, transfer (including a case where after retirement the person is reappointed as a teacher or staff on the retirement date or the following day without receiving retirement benefits and retirement allowance; hereafter the same shall apply), leave of absence, or any other change, the head of the relevant school institution shall submit a report on the change in status to the TP without delay; provided, where the head of a school institution receiving the transfer submits a transfer-in report to the TP, the transfer-out report for the relevant teacher or staff shall not be submitted.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

  (2) The amount to be transferred to the TP by the Government Employees Pension Service or the Minister of National Defense pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be the amount of benefits payable under the Public Officials Pension Act or the Military Pension Act as of the date of retirement or death of the teachers and staff pursuant to Article 52-2 of the Act. Benefits pursuant to Article 38 of the Act, benefits paid in lieu of a pension pursuant to Article 36 of the Act on pension as applied, and retirement survivors' pension additional amount and retirement survivors' pension special additional amount pursuant to Article 54 of the Act on pension as applied shall be transferred by March 31 of the relevant year for payments made from September of the preceding year through February of the relevant year and by September 30 of the relevant year for payments made from March through August of the relevant year.

CHAPTER VI REQUEST FOR REVIEW

Article 76 (Organization of the Review Committee on Pension Benefits for Private School Teachers) (1) The Review Committee on Pension Benefits for Private School Teachers established under Article 53 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Review Committee") shall be composed of 9 members. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Feb. 28, 2000>
  (2) The members in paragraph (1) shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Education from among public officials of Grade 5 or higher in the Ministry of Education (including general service public officials belonging to the Senior Executive Service), supervisors of education, and persons with extensive learning and experience in the medical field, the legal profession, or social security. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1982; Feb. 1, 1991; Jan. 29, 2001; Jun. 12, 2006; Jan. 24, 2007; Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 77 (Term of office of members) (1) The term of office of a member shall be 3 years, except when a member who is a public official retires or is transferred.
  (2) The term of office of a substitute member shall be the remaining term of the predecessor.
  (3) A member may be reappointed.

Article 78 (Chairperson) (1) The Review Committee shall have 1 chairperson, who shall be elected from among the members. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>
  (2) The chairperson shall preside over and supervise the affairs of the Review Committee, and where the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated by the chairperson shall act on his or her behalf. <Amended on Feb. 24, 2003; Jul. 2, 2019>

Article 79 (Resolutions) (1) Meetings of the Review Committee shall be convened by the chairperson. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>
  (2) Meetings of the Review Committee shall pass a resolution with the attendance of a majority of the incumbent members and the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Feb. 24, 2003>

Article 80 (Secretariat of the Committee and allowances for members) (1) To handle the administrative affairs of the Review Committee, the Review Committee shall have 1 secretary-general and several clerks, and the secretary-general and clerks shall be appointed from among the employees of the TP by the chairperson of the TP. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010; Jul. 2, 2019>
  (2) The TP shall pay allowances to members who attend meetings of the Review Committee (excluding members who are executive officers or employees of the TP) within the budgetary limits. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (3) Matters necessary for the operation of the Review Committee shall be determined by the chairperson, undergoing a resolution of the Review Committee. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>

Article 81 (Procedure for filing request for review) (1) A person who has an objection to a decision on benefits, the collection of contributions, or any other decision on benefits under the Act and intends to file a request for review with the Review Committee pursuant to Article 53(1) of the Act shall submit a request for review, together with a statement of reasons, to the TP within the period prescribed in Article 53(2) of the Act. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Jan. 29, 1988; Jan. 1, 2010>
  (2) The TP shall, within 10 days from the date it receives the request for review under paragraph (1), request a review by submitting the request for review to the Review Committee, together with a written reply and other necessary documents. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>

Article 82 (Supplementation of request and dismissal of request) (1) Where the Review Committee finds matters requiring supplementation in a request for review under Article 81(1) or a written reply under paragraph (2) of that Article, it shall set a period for supplementation and request the claimant or the TP to supplement them.
  (2) Where the claimant fails to supplement within the period for supplementation under paragraph (1) and the review cannot be conducted based solely on the facts stated in the request for review, the Review Committee may dismiss the request.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Sep. 18, 2018]

Article 83 (Notice to interested parties) (1) Where a request for review is filed under Article 81, the Review Committee shall notify the teachers and staff, the head of the relevant school institution, and other interested parties concerned with the relevant request for review. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>
  (2) A person who has received the notice under paragraph (1) may state his or her opinion on the relevant case to the Review Committee. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>

Article 84 (Submission of reports or statements of opinion) Where the Review Committee deems it necessary for the review, it may require the person who filed the request for review or other interested parties to submit reports or state their opinions, or may require them to appear and ask questions. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>

Article 85 (Decision on review) (1) A decision on review shall be made in writing. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>
  (2) The written decision under paragraph (1) shall state the disposition and the reasons, be signed or sealed by the chairperson and the members who attended the meeting, and a copy thereof shall be sent to the claimant, the head of the relevant school institution, and other interested parties. <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018>

Article 86 (Effect of decision) Any matter decided by the Review Committee shall take effect from the time when a certified copy of the written decision is served on the claimant. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984>

Article 87 (Reimbursement of actual costs of interested parties) The TP shall reimburse actual costs to interested parties who attend the Review Committee pursuant to Article 84. <Amended on Dec. 31, 1984; Jan. 1, 2010>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation, on condition that it starts to apply from January 1, 1984.
Article 2 (Procedures for retroactive aggregation of periods of service)
(1) Where a teacher or staff member intends to obtain aggregation of periods of service pursuant to Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act on Partial Amendment of the Private School Teachers' Pension Act (Act No. 3684), he or she shall submit an application for retroactive aggregation of periods of service (including an application in the form of an electronic document; hereinafter the same shall apply) specifying the periods of service to be aggregated, together with documents certifying the fact of working at the relevant school institution, to the head of the affiliated school institution. <Amended on Jan. 24, 2007>
(2) Where the head of the school institution receives an application under paragraph (1), he or she shall forward it to the Management Corporation within 7 days, and in cases where the applicant intends to have the period of continuous service at the school institution at which he or she is in service at the time of application aggregated as a period of service, a written consent of the head of the relevant school management body shall be submitted together.
(3) The Management Corporation that receives an application forwarded under paragraph (2) shall investigate the aggregated period and other necessary matters, determine whether to approve aggregation of periods of service, and notify the applicant and the head of the relevant school institution of the result.
Article 3 (Method of lump-sum payment of retroactively paid contributions)
Where a teacher or staff member who is paying or intends to pay retroactive contributions for a period approved for retroactive aggregation pursuant to Article 2(3) of the Addenda intends to pay in a lump sum the contributions corresponding to the remaining period of service to be retroactively aggregated, he or she shall pay the personal contributions corresponding to such period to the head of the affiliated school institution, and the head of the affiliated school institution shall pay the received personal contributions (or, in cases falling under the proviso of the main clause of Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act on Partial Amendment of the Private School Teachers' Pension Act (Act No. 3684), the contributions borne by the relevant teacher or staff member) and the corporate contributions under the main clause of Article 2 of the Addenda to the Act on Partial Amendment of the Private School Teachers' Pension Act to the pension collection institution at the time of payment of the next contributions.
Article 4 (Measures against delinquency in payment of retroactive contributions)
Where a person who has obtained approval for retroactive aggregation of periods of service pursuant to Article 2(3) of the Addenda fails to pay retroactive contributions for 6 months or more, the Management Corporation may revoke the approval for retroactive aggregation of periods of service for the period corresponding to the delinquent amount.
